All estimates are signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger dependency / more negative dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker dependency / less negative or higher dependency score in the exposed group.\n\nThe next highest-value discoveries are not another broad set of null direct-target tests, but context-robustness checks that ask whether the leading associations survive under higher screen quality and in biologically/technically important strata. I registered four screen-quality refinements using eligibility screen_roc_auc >= 0.95, roughly a high-quality-screen subset near the median or above. The scientific hypothesis is that if these effects are not screen-quality artifacts, they should remain near the large 0.75-0.85 signed range among higher-quality screens. If an effect collapses toward zero in the high-quality subset, the claim should be interpreted as restricted to lower-quality or heterogeneous screen contexts; if it persists, the dataset association becomes harder to attribute to assay noise.\n\nFor USP7/TP53-wild-type, I added aneuploidy strata because TP53 loss is commonly associated with aneuploidy and copy-number instability. The high-aneuploidy and low-aneuploidy refinements test whether the USP7 effect is merely a byproduct of the co-occurrence of TP53 loss and aneuploidy, or whether it remains detectable within relatively homogeneous aneuploidy strata. Persistence in both strata would strengthen the USP7 association within this dataset, while strong attenuation would indicate context specificity.\n\nFor WRN/MSI-high, I added a higher-mutation-burden refinement with mutation_burden >= 10. H17 already showed the association remains when the comparator population has mutation burden at least 4, and it independently validated. This stricter test asks whether the MSI-high WRN effect is especially robust among MSI-high-like high-TMB lines rather than being driven by contrast against very low mutation-burden comparator lines. If the effect remains near 0.75-0.85, it further supports H9, for which direct independent validation remains the main next priority.\n\nI also added one focused broad exploration: RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency. RB1 loss can promote chromosomal instability and mitotic stress, and KIF18A contributes to chromosome congression and mitotic fidelity. The directional hypothesis is that RB1-loss cells show stronger KIF18A dependency (direction -1, positive signed estimate), although the same-gene/pathway target dependencies have generally been null in this dataset. record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency / more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency / less negative or higher score in the exposed group.

The batch_a robustness results support all four leading accepted associations. H62, USP7 dependency comparing TP53-wild-type with TP53-loss within screen_batch=batch_a, gave +0.789 (95% interval +0.749 to +0.828). This is far from zero and essentially matches the overall H6 discovery estimate. H64, SMARCA2 dependency with SMARCA4 loss in batch_a, gave +0.747 (0.709 to 0.785), slightly lower than the overall H7 estimate but still a very large association and far from zero. H66, WRN dependency with MSI-high in batch_a, gave +0.824 (0.766 to 0.882) despite only 37 MSI-high cells in batch_a; the interval is wide but very large and excludes zero. H68, NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss in batch_a in the reversed direction, gave +0.812 (0.765 to 0.858), indicating weaker NFE2L2 dependency / higher score in KEAP1-loss cells and supporting H13.

The high-screen-quality subset, defined by screen_roc_auc >= 0.95, also supports the same four effects. H70 USP7/TP53-wild-type was +0.804 (0.780 to 0.828). H71 SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss was +0.790 (0.765 to 0.816). H72 WRN/MSI-high was +0.795 (0.758 to 0.832). H73 NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss was +0.790 (0.763 to 0.816). These estimates are not attenuated toward zero and are consistent with the leading overall effects, making it less plausible that these are artifacts of low screen quality or noisy screens. Multiplicity remains a consideration for context tests, but the consistency across independent technical contexts and the magnitude relative to the dependency-score standard deviations are compelling within this dataset.

The USP7 aneuploidy-strata results further reduce concern that the TP53-wild-type/USP7 association is merely a byproduct of co-occurring aneuploidy. In high aneuploidy, H74 gave +0.801 (0.758 to 0.844); in low aneuploidy, H75 gave +0.816 (0.785 to 0.846). These intervals overlap and remain very large. H76 also strengthens WRN/MSI-high: in the stricter mutation_burden >= 10 stratum, the signed estimate was +0.768 (0.721 to 0.815), still extremely large, even when the comparator population is itself relatively high-mutation-burden. This supports H9 without establishing causality or external generalizability.

The one focused new broad hypothesis, H77 RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency, is rejected: signed estimate +0.008 (interval -0.019 to +0.036). This is null and not scientifically meaningful given the KIF18A dependency-score scale. Like many other targeted same-gene or pathway-target hypotheses tested so far, it does not show a large measured predictor effect.

Given the new robustness evidence, I request independent validation of H9, the unrestricted WRN/MSI-high association. H9 is now supported by discovery, non-KY library robustness, adherent-culture robustness, batch_a, high screen quality, high mutation burden, and validation of the related H17 restricted claim, but it remains the only leading accepted main effect without direct independent validation. If validation confirms, H9 can be closed as a robust within-dataset association; if validation attenuates, the WRN claim should be narrowed to the specific contexts where it remains large. These findings remain associations within this supplied lung-cell-line dataset, not causal mechanisms or clinically validated biomarker claims.

The scientific hypothesis is that if these effects are not screen-quality artifacts, they should remain near the large 0.75-0.85 signed range among higher-quality screens. record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, that is a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group relative to comparator; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency, that is a higher or less negative score in the exposed group.

Due evidence assessment. H9, the unrestricted WRN dependency comparison MSI-high versus not MSI-high, received independent validation R63: signed estimate +0.7896 with independent interval +0.7364 to +0.8429. Discovery R9 was +0.7899, interval +0.7604 to +0.8193. These are nearly identical and extremely large relative to the WRN dependency-score distribution, whose standard deviation is about 0.263. The validation interval remains far from zero even with the validation alpha accounting for multiple validation comparisons. I therefore accept H9 and close its investigation. The within-dataset claim is that MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency than non-MSI-high cells.

H17, WRN dependency among mutation_burden >= 4, had validation deadline R39. Validation gave +0.8187, independent interval +0.7695 to +0.8680, closely aligned with discovery R17 +0.7869, interval +0.7567 to +0.8171. This confirms the high-mutation-burden-restricted WRN/MSI-high association and supports, but does not replace, H9 as the main WRN finding. H17 remains accepted and closed.

H13, the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss claim, had validation deadline R38. Validation gave +0.8020, independent interval +0.7746 to +0.8294, while discovery R10 gave signed +0.7961, interval +0.7759 to +0.8163. Because direction +1 was registered to capture the reverse of the original mechanistic guess, a positive estimate means KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. higher or less negative dependency scores, than KEAP1-intact cells. This direction is counterintuitive but stable across discovery and validation and across several context checks. I accept H13 and close it.

Synthesis of the current evidence: the strongest supported findings are four large measured predictor-outcome associations, now all directly independently validated within the supplied dataset or through the corresponding validated main claim. TP53-wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency (H6, validation R50 +0.811). SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7, validation R13 +0.805). MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency (H9, validation R63 +0.790; H17 also validated +0.819 in the mutation_burden >= 4 population). KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, or higher NFE2L2 dependency score, than KEAP1-intact cells (H13, validation R38 +0.802; H10 in the opposite direction is rejected because the raw contrast points the other way).

These effects are scientifically meaningful within this dataset. The leading signed differences are roughly 0.75 to 0.82 dependency-score units, which is more than two standard deviations of the relevant dependency-score distributions and very far from zero. Interpreting them literally as percentages is awkward because dependency scores are often negative, but they are plainly larger than any plausible 10 percent clinical-significance threshold if judged on the outcome scale. The supporting context evidence is also unusually consistent: the four leading associations remain large in non-KY and KY CRISPR libraries, adherent culture, the largest screen batch, high screen-quality screens, different mutation-burden contexts, and both high- and low-aneuploidy strata for USP7.

The negative findings are an important part of the report. Direct same-gene or pathway-target hypotheses are broadly unsupported in this dataset: KRAS mutation did not predict KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E did not predict BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification did not predict EGFR dependency, including among KRAS/BRAF wild-type cells; ERBB2 amplification did not predict ERBB2 dependency; PIK3CA mutation did not predict STAT3 dependency; MYC amplification did not predict POLR2A dependency; high MYC expression did not support RPL11; TP53 loss did not predict MDM2 dependency; MSI-high did not predict DHX9 or KIF18A dependency; KRAS mutation did not show the predicted RIT1 pattern among BRAF wild-type cells; ERBB2 amplification did not predict TMED10 dependency; and RB1 loss did not predict KIF18A dependency. Interaction tests so far have not shown meaningful modification of the leading SMARCA2 or NFE2L2 associations by ARID1A loss or TP53-loss status. Formal batch and lineage interactions remain registered but unresolved; however, the main effects are already robust within batch_a, adenocarcinoma, library, culture, screen-quality, and mutation-burden contexts, and the direct validation of H9 closes the most important remaining gap.

Unresolved uncertainty is now primarily interpretive and external, not statistical. These are associations within the supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset. They do not establish causality, mechanistic synthetic lethality, drug response, or clinical biomarker behavior. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction is especially biologically counterintuitive and may reflect dataset-specific structure, co-alteration patterns, scoring behavior, or some unmeasured confounder. Likewise, USP7/TP53-wild-type could reflect genuine biology or co-occurring genomic/assay structure; the aneuploidy-strata results reduce one specific confounding concern but do not prove mechanism. Generalizability outside this dataset, lineage, screen library, culture setting, and batch structure remains untested.

Most informative next analysis: because all leading main effects are validated, the next high-value work is to (1) formally test major technical modifiers of the validated effects, starting with library-specific heterogeneity as registered in the current proposal batch, and (2) probe additional biologically plausible predictor-outcome pairs, especially DNA-repair/mitotic-stress hypotheses such as BRCA2 loss for WRN, DHX9, KIF18A, and POLR2A, plus STK11 loss for KRAS dependency. If a new context or predictor estimate approaches the magnitude of the leading validated effects and is not already explained by the accepted associations, it would merit validation; otherwise, the current within-dataset conclusion is four robust dependency-score associations and a broad null result for many direct-target dependency predictions.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Third, for WRN/MSI-high, I test persistence within TP53-loss lines. This is biologically interesting because TP53 loss alters DNA-repair and replication-stress biology; if MSI-high still shows strong WRN dependency among TP53-loss lines, the MSI-WRN association is not confined to TP53-intact contexts. CDKN2A loss is tested against POLR2A dependency because cell-cycle checkpoint loss and increased proliferative pressure can increase transcriptional demand. Modest estimates with intervals excluding zero should still be interpreted cautiously because many context and predictor hypotheses create multiplicity. In this explore stage I defer the four library-interaction tests H78 through H81 and one lower-priority BRCA2/KIF18A test H84 so that the next analysis batch can prioritize two scientific goals: testing whether the four leading validated associations persist inside specific co-alteration contexts, and probing new biologically motivated predictor-outcome pairs beyond direct same-gene dependency predictions. I accept H13 and close it.\n\nSynthesis of the current evidence: the strongest supported findings are four large measured predictor-outcome associations, now all directly independently validated within the supplied dataset or through the corresponding validated main claim. Interpreting them literally as percentages is awkward because dependency scores are often negative, but they are plainly larger than any plausible 10 percent clinical-significance threshold if judged on the outcome scale. The supporting context evidence is also unusually consistent: the four leading associations remain large in non-KY and KY CRISPR libraries, adherent culture, the largest screen batch, high screen-quality screens, different mutation-burden contexts, and both high- and low-aneuploidy strata for USP7.\n\nThe negative findings are an important part of the report. Direct same-gene or pathway-target hypotheses are broadly unsupported in this dataset: KRAS mutation did not predict KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E did not predict BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification did not predict EGFR dependency, including among KRAS/BRAF wild-type cells; ERBB2 amplification did not predict ERBB2 dependency; PIK3CA mutation did not predict STAT3 dependency; MYC amplification did not predict POLR2A dependency; high MYC expression did not support RPL11; TP53 loss did not predict MDM2 dependency; MSI-high did not predict DHX9 or KIF18A dependency; KRAS mutation did not show the predicted RIT1 pattern among BRAF wild-type cells; ERBB2 amplification did not predict TMED10 dependency; and RB1 loss did not predict KIF18A dependency. Interaction tests so far have not shown meaningful modification of the leading SMARCA2 or NFE2L2 associations by ARID1A loss or TP53-loss status. Formal batch and lineage interactions remain registered but unresolved; however, the main effects are already robust within batch_a, adenocarcinoma, library, culture, screen-quality, and mutation-burden contexts, and the direct validation of H9 closes the most important remaining gap.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty is now primarily interpretive and external, not statistical. These are associations within the supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset. They do not establish causality, mechanistic synthetic lethality, drug response, or clinical biomarker behavior. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction is especially biologically counterintuitive and may reflect dataset-specific structure, co-alteration patterns, scoring behavior, or some unmeasured confounder. Likewise, USP7/TP53-wild-type could reflect genuine biology or co-occurring genomic/assay structure; the aneuploidy-strata results reduce one specific confounding concern but do not prove mechanism. Generalizability outside this dataset, lineage, screen library, culture setting, and batch structure remains untested.\n\nMost informative next analysis: because all leading main effects are validated, the next high-value work is to (1) formally test major technical modifiers of the validated effects, starting with library-specific heterogeneity as registered in the current proposal batch, and (2) probe additional biologically plausible predictor-outcome pairs, especially DNA-repair/mitotic-stress hypotheses such as BRCA2 loss for WRN, DHX9, KIF18A, and POLR2A, plus STK11 loss for KRAS dependency. If a new context or predictor estimate approaches the magnitude of the leading validated effects and is not already explained by the accepted associations, it would merit validation; otherwise, the current within-dataset conclusion is four robust dependency-score associations and a broad null result for many direct-target dependency predictions."}}

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
All new estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency or a higher dependency score in the exposed group. The BRCA2-loss hypotheses are null across the DNA-repair/replication-stress genes tested here: H82 WRN, estimate +0.00007 with interval -0.045 to +0.045; H83 DHX9, +0.012 with interval -0.020 to +0.044; and H85 POLR2A, +0.013 with interval -0.019 to +0.046. These are within the usual null band and do not support strong biological effects despite mechanistic plausibility. I reject and close them. Likewise, the STK11-loss broad predictors are null for KRAS dependency, H86 estimate -0.002 with interval -0.022 to +0.018; for POLR2A dependency, H91 estimate +0.011 with interval -0.008 to +0.031; and for RPL11 dependency, H92 estimate -0.012 with interval -0.033 to +0.009. The CDKN2A-loss hypothesis against POLR2A is also null, H93 estimate +0.002 with interval -0.018 to +0.022. All are rejected and closed. These results extend the broader pattern that most direct or plausible gene-alteration dependency predictions in this dataset are small or absent, whereas a small set of very large associations dominate the dependency landscape.

The co-alteration persistence tests support the leading accepted effects. H87, USP7 dependency among TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss cells restricted to KEAP1-loss cells, gave +0.794 with interval +0.754 to +0.834, essentially matching the overall USP7/TP53-wild-type effect. H88, SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-loss versus intact cells restricted to STK11-loss cells, gave +0.769 with interval +0.727 to +0.811, also close to the overall SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss effect. H89, WRN dependency among MSI-high versus non-MSI-high cells restricted to TP53-loss cells, gave +0.833 with interval +0.765 to +0.900. The MSI-high/TP53-loss cell is small, with only 24 exposed observations, so the interval is wide, but the effect remains far from zero. H90, the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss effect restricted to STK11-loss cells, gave +0.775 with interval +0.727 to +0.823, again supporting the counterintuitive direction that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These context checks make it less plausible that the leading associations are carried entirely by one co-occurring alteration context, but they remain within-dataset associations, not causal claims. I accept and close H87-H90.

The one genuinely new positive finding is H94: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319, in 266 versus 1734 cell lines. This is not in the huge +0.75 to +0.85 range of the leading four effects, but it is still substantial on the dependency-score scale: the STAT3 dependency-score standard deviation is about 0.246, so this difference is roughly one standard deviation and is far beyond the null band seen in other predictor tests. The interval excludes zero and the sample sizes are adequate. Given the large number of comparisons tested, however, I cannot yet regard it as equally secure as the validated main effects. Its magnitude is scientifically meaningful, but its status should be tested independently. Therefore I accept H94 as a promising within-dataset association, keep its investigation active, and request independent validation of H94.

The main alternative explanations for H94 are residual confounding by correlated genomic or expression features, multiplicity across many null predictor-outcome tests, and dataset-specific biological structure. PTEN loss may co-occur with pathways that alter STAT3 dependency, or it may reflect a broader PTEN/PI3K/mTOR/STAT signaling axis. These findings remain associations measured in the supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset; they do not establish causality, drug sensitivity, or external clinical generalizability. I have registered follow-up tests for PTEN/STAT3 robustness and modification, including interaction by TP53 loss, persistence in high-quality screens, and persistence in KRAS-wild-type and non-KY-library contexts.

For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group relative to comparator. For direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency or a higher, less negative dependency score in the exposed group.  Due assessment H6: TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss status associated with stronger USP7 dependency received independent validation R50: signed estimate +0.8115 with independent interval +0.7821 to +0.8408 at the validation-adjusted level. This matches discovery R6 +0.8019 and is far beyond the small null band seen in rejected predictor tests. H6 is accepted and closed as a robust within-dataset association.  Due assessment H94: PTEN loss versus PTEN-intact status associated with stronger STAT3 dependency received independent validation R76: signed estimate +0.2919 with independent interval +0.2135 to +0.3704. This is concordant with discovery R75 +0.2674, interval +0.2153 to +0.3195. The validation interval excludes zero even with the stricter independent interval. The effect is smaller than the leading four associations but is still scientifically meaningful on the dependency-score scale: dependency_STAT3 has SD about 0.246, so the effect is roughly 1.2 SD, and the lower confidence bound is roughly 0.9 SD. Thus I accept H94 as a newly supported within-dataset association but keep its investigation active pending robustness and specificity checks.  Due assessment H16: the ARID1A-loss interaction in the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency comparison received independent validation R77: signed estimate +0.0162 with interval -0.0543 to +0.0868. Discovery R16 was +0.0373 with interval -0.0148 to +0.0894. Both are small and compatible with no meaningful modification, especially relative to the huge main SMARCA4-loss effect around +0.78 to +0.81. I reject H16 and close it. This supports interpreting H7 as a broad SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association not materially modified by ARID1A loss in this dataset.  Synthesis of supported findings: the strongest within-dataset predictor-outcome associations are now (1) TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency, (2) SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, (3) MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency, including the mutation_burden >= 4 restriction, and (4) KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, meaning higher or less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores than KEAP1-intact cells. These four are independently validated and remain large across libraries, culture, batch_a, high screen quality, mutation-burden contexts, aneuploidy strata for USP7, and several co-alteration restrictions. The new fifth supported association is PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, discovery and validation estimates near +0.27 to +0.29. This is smaller than the leading four but well above the usual null band and above plausible clinical-scale thresholds if dependency-score units are interpreted directly.  Negative findings are substantial: direct same-gene or pathway-target dependency predictions were broadly null, including KRAS mutation/KRAS, BRAF V600E/BRAF, EGFR amplification/EGFR even among KRAS/BRAF wild-type contexts, ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2, PIK3CA/STAT3, MYC/POLR2A, high MYC/RPL11, TP53 loss/MDM2, MSI-high/DHX9, MSI-high/KIF18A, KRAS/RIT1, ERBB2/TMED10, RB1/KIF18A, MYC/MDM2 among TP53-WT, BRCA2 loss with WRN/DHX9/POLR2A, STK11 loss with KRAS/POLR2A/RPL11, and CDKN2A loss with POLR2A. Interaction tests have not shown meaningful modification of the leading associations by ARID1A loss or TP53-loss status, and ARID1A modification of SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss is now independently null.  Unresolved uncertainty is mainly interpretive and external. The accepted effects are measured associations within this supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset. They do not prove causality, mechanistic synthetic lethality, drug response, or clinical biomarker behavior. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction remains biologically counterintuitive and could reflect dataset-specific structure, co-alteration patterns, scoring behavior, or confounding. USP7/TP53-wild-type and PTEN/STAT3 could also reflect correlated genomic or pathway features. The most informative next analysis is to complete the PTEN/STAT3 robustness battery: interaction by TP53 loss, high-quality screens, KRAS wild-type, non-KY library, batch_a, adherent culture, adenocarcinoma subtype, and MYC-amplification interaction, plus one specificity check using PTEN loss against KRAS dependency. If PTEN/STAT3 persists across these contexts, it should be closed as a fifth robust within-dataset association; if it attenuates in key subsets, the claim should be narrowed to the context in which it remains large. Formal library, batch, and lineage interaction tests for the leading four effects remain secondary because their main effects are already robust in those subset analyses.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

For direction -1 loss or mutation claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group than in the comparator. For TP53-wild-type claims, where exposed=0 and comparator=1, a positive estimate means TP53-wild-type cells have a more negative dependency score than TP53-loss cells. The leading validated associations are still the four very large effects: TP53-wild-type stronger USP7, SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2, MSI-high stronger WRN, and KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2. The newly validated moderate association is PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, about +0.27 to +0.29 signed units, roughly one SD of STAT3 dependency. The next scientific priority is to determine whether PTEN/STAT3 is context-specific but robust, whether it is specific to STAT3 or reflects a broader PTEN effect, and whether other predictors also predict STAT3.  I register a STAT3-centered predictor battery because STAT3 now has a moderate independently validated association and is biologically interpretable as a signaling dependency node. PIK3CA mutation among PTEN-wild-type cells tests whether a related PI3K-pathway alteration predicts STAT3 when PTEN is intact; this helps distinguish a PTEN-specific STAT3 association from a broader PI3K/STAT3 axis, while avoiding dependence on possibly rare PTEN/PIK3CA co-alteration cells. TP53-wild-type status is tested because TP53-wild-type is the strongest USP7 predictor and could confound PTEN/STAT3 if correlated with TP53 status. SMARCA4-loss, MSI-high, and KEAP1-loss are tested against STAT3 to see whether the major tumor suppressor or genomic markers are broadly associated with dependency scores or remain specific to their accepted outcomes. MYC amplification, APC mutation, NF1 loss, and SMAD4 loss are added as plausible but not yet tested signaling or genomic predictors; any large positive STAT3 estimate would be a candidate sixth major association, but would require independent validation before acceptance.  I also register PTEN-loss specificity tests against USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN. These are not meant to change the PTEN/STAT3 claim but to ask whether PTEN loss predicts the other leading dependencies. If PTEN loss is null for USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN, that strengthens specificity of the PTEN/STAT3 finding. If it is large for several dependencies, PTEN loss may reflect a broader stress or proliferation-associated dependency phenotype rather than STAT3-specific biology.  These proposals deliberately leave the PTEN/STAT3 robustness battery H95-H103 active and add only focused refinements. Direct-target tests have largely been null, and leading effects have already shown stability across libraries, culture, batch_a, screen quality, and several co-alteration contexts. Therefore broad interaction testing for the four leading effects is lower priority than understanding specificity and possible confounding around PTEN/STAT3, while still allowing discovery of another strong predictor if one appears. No validation is requested at this explore stage.

Iteration 7/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The newly validated moderate association is PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, about +0.27 to +0.29 signed units, roughly one SD of STAT3 dependency. The next scientific priority is to determine whether PTEN/STAT3 is context-specific but robust, whether it is specific to STAT3 or reflects a broader PTEN effect, and whether other predictors also predict STAT3.  I register a STAT3-centered predictor battery because STAT3 now has a moderate independently validated association and is biologically interpretable as a signaling dependency node. PIK3CA mutation among PTEN-wild-type cells tests whether a related PI3K-pathway alteration predicts STAT3 when PTEN is intact; this helps distinguish a PTEN-specific STAT3 association from a broader PI3K/STAT3 axis, while avoiding dependence on possibly rare PTEN/PIK3CA co-alteration cells. TP53-wild-type status is tested because TP53-wild-type is the strongest USP7 predictor and could confound PTEN/STAT3 if correlated with TP53 status. SMARCA4-loss, MSI-high, and KEAP1-loss are tested against STAT3 to see whether the major tumor suppressor or genomic markers are broadly associated with dependency scores or remain specific to their accepted outcomes. MYC amplification, APC mutation, NF1 loss, and SMAD4 loss are added as plausible but not yet tested signaling or genomic predictors; any large positive STAT3 estimate would be a candidate sixth major association, but would require independent validation before acceptance.  I also register PTEN-loss specificity tests against USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN. These are not meant to change the PTEN/STAT3 claim but to ask whether PTEN loss predicts the other leading dependencies. If PTEN loss is null for USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN, that strengthens specificity of the PTEN/STAT3 finding. If it is large for several dependencies, PTEN loss may reflect a broader stress or proliferation-associated dependency phenotype rather than STAT3-specific biology.  These proposals deliberately leave the PTEN/STAT3 robustness battery H95-H103 active and add only focused refinements. Direct-target tests have largely been null, and leading effects have already shown stability across libraries, culture, batch_a, screen quality, and several co-alteration contexts. Therefore broad interaction testing for the four leading effects is lower priority than understanding specificity and possible confounding around PTEN/STAT3, while still allowing discovery of another strong predictor if one appears. These are falsifiable independence checks: persistence near the current +0.75 to +0.85 signed range would reduce concern that the main association is carried entirely by that co-alteration context, while attenuation would require narrowing the main claim to co-alteration-specific settings. The second group tests new biologically motivated predictor-outcome pairs. STK11 loss is tested against KRAS, POLR2A, and RPL11 dependency because STK11/LKB1 loss can alter metabolic stress and biosynthetic signaling. CDKN2A loss is tested against POLR2A dependency and PTEN loss against STAT3 dependency as additional plausible checkpoint/signaling hypotheses. The BRCA2-loss hypotheses are null across the DNA-repair/replication-stress genes tested here: H82 WRN, estimate +0.00007 with interval -0.045 to +0.045; H83 DHX9, +0.012 with interval -0.020 to +0.044; and H85 POLR2A, +0.013 with interval -0.019 to +0.046. These are within the usual null band and do not support strong biological effects despite mechanistic plausibility. I reject and close them. Likewise, the STK11-loss broad predictors are null for KRAS dependency, H86 estimate -0.002 with interval -0.022 to +0.018; for POLR2A dependency, H91 estimate +0.011 with interval -0.008 to +0.031; and for RPL11 dependency, H92 estimate -0.012 with interval -0.033 to +0.009. The CDKN2A-loss hypothesis against POLR2A is also null, H93 estimate +0.002 with interval -0.018 to +0.022. All are rejected and closed. These results extend the broader pattern that most direct or plausible gene-alteration dependency predictions in this dataset are small or absent, whereas a small set of very large associations dominate the dependency landscape.\n\nThe co-alteration persistence tests support the leading accepted effects. H87, USP7 dependency among TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss cells restricted to KEAP1-loss cells, gave +0.794 with interval +0.754 to +0.834, essentially matching the overall USP7/TP53-wild-type effect. H88, SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-loss versus intact cells restricted to STK11-loss cells, gave +0.769 with interval +0.727 to +0.811, also close to the overall SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss effect. H89, WRN dependency among MSI-high versus non-MSI-high cells restricted to TP53-loss cells, gave +0.833 with interval +0.765 to +0.900. The MSI-high/TP53-loss cell is small, with only 24 exposed observations, so the interval is wide, but the effect remains far from zero. H90, the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss effect restricted to STK11-loss cells, gave +0.775 with interval +0.727 to +0.823, again supporting the counterintuitive direction that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These context checks make it less plausible that the leading associations are carried entirely by one co-occurring alteration context, but they remain within-dataset associations, not causal claims. I accept and close H87-H90.\n\nThe one genuinely new positive finding is H94: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319, in 266 versus 1734 cell lines. record.narrative: This batch prioritizes completion of the PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency robustness and specificity program, because H94 is now the only independently validated moderate new association and its interpretation depends on whether it is stable across technical and biological contexts and specific to STAT3. All selected claims are direction -1. For main effects, a positive signed estimate means PTEN-loss cells have stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative dependency score, than PTEN-intact cells. For the interaction claims H95 and H102, a positive signed estimate means the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency is larger in the named subgroup than in its complement. H95 and H102 test whether TP53-loss status or MYC amplification materially modifies the PTEN/STAT3 effect. Because the main PTEN/STAT3 estimate is about +0.27 to +0.29, I will consider an interaction scientifically important only if it is appreciably smaller than the main effect and remains compatible with meaningful modification; small interactions with intervals overlapping zero should be treated as no meaningful modification. H96, H97, H98, H99, H100, and H101 test persistence in high-quality screens, KRAS-wild-type cells, non-KY library cells, batch_a, adherent culture, and adenocarcinoma subtype, respectively. If the PTEN/STAT3 effect remains clearly positive and near the overall magnitude in these strata, the finding becomes less plausibly driven by screen quality, a single library, a batch, culture format, KRAS context, or lineage subtype. H103, H113, H114, and H115 test whether PTEN loss also predicts KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, or WRN dependency. These are specificity checks: PTEN loss should be null or very small for these other leading dependency outcomes if H94 reflects STAT3-related biology rather than a broad dependency-stress phenotype. A large positive estimate on one or more of these specificity claims would require reinterpreting PTEN loss as a broader dependency predictor or as a proxy for correlated genomic features. No validation is requested at this stage because these are discovery-context robustness tests; validation should be considered later only for new claims that are both large and not already covered by the existing H94 validation.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 main effects, a positive estimate means PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells, i.e. a more negative dependency score. For direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate means the PTEN-loss effect is larger in the named subgroup than in its complement. The interaction H95, testing whether TP53 loss modifies PTEN/STAT3 dependency, gave R78 estimate -0.0967 with 95% interval -0.2171 to +0.0236 in cells with 54 versus 352 observations in the TP53-loss stratum and 212 versus 1382 in the complement. The signed estimate is opposite the registered positive-interaction direction and the interval includes zero, so I reject the claim of positive modification. The negative point estimate raises the possibility that PTEN loss is associated with a smaller STAT3 effect among TP53-loss cells, but the interaction is too imprecise to conclude either attenuation or no modification. I registered direct PTEN-loss effects within TP53-loss and TP53-intact strata to characterize this context more clearly. The MYC-amplification interaction H102, R85 estimate +0.0308 with interval -0.1011 to +0.1627, is small and includes zero, so I reject meaningful positive modification and close it. The context robustness tests support the overall PTEN/STAT3 association. In high-quality screens H96 gave +0.2394, interval +0.1730 to +0.3059; KRAS-wild-type cells H97 gave +0.2726, interval +0.2129 to +0.3323; non-KY library cells H98 gave +0.3020, interval +0.2409 to +0.3632; batch_a H99 gave +0.2337, interval +0.1252 to +0.3421; adherent culture H100 gave +0.2619, interval +0.2027 to +0.3211; and adenocarcinoma subtype H101 gave +0.2677, interval +0.2058 to +0.3295. These intervals all exclude zero and remain near the overall effect magnitude, although H99 is wider because the PTEN-loss cell has only 63 observations. The specificity tests are null or very small. PTEN loss against KRAS dependency H103 gave -0.0135, interval -0.0345 to +0.0076; against USP7 H113 gave +0.0173, interval -0.0308 to +0.0654; against SMARCA2 H114 gave +0.0180, interval -0.0288 to +0.0647; and against WRN H115 gave +0.0033, interval -0.0314 to +0.0380. These are within the usual null band and are orders of magnitude smaller than the leading USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 effects. They do not support PTEN loss as a broad dependency predictor for the other leading outcomes. I reject these specificity alternatives and close them. Taken together with the already validated main PTEN/STAT3 association R75/R76, the positive technical and biological stratum estimates, the absence of meaningful MYC interaction, and the null specificity tests, H94 can be accepted and closed as a robust within-dataset association. The direct TP53-loss stratum question remains worth refining because H95 suggested possible attenuation, but it does not negate the overall PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association measured in this dataset. These are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal claims, drug-response claims, or externally generalizable biomarker statements. No new validation request is needed: the main H94 claim has already been independently validated, and additional stratum-specific validation would add little relative to completing direct TP53-context estimates.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

For direction -1 loss or mutation claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group than in the comparator. For TP53-wild-type claims, where exposed=0 and comparator=1, a positive estimate means TP53-wild-type cells have a more negative dependency score than TP53-loss cells. The leading validated associations are still the four very large effects: TP53-wild-type stronger USP7, SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2, MSI-high stronger WRN, and KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2. The newly validated moderate association is PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, about +0.27 to +0.29 signed units, roughly one SD of STAT3 dependency. The next scientific priority is to determine whether PTEN/STAT3 is context-specific but robust, whether it is specific to STAT3 or reflects a broader PTEN effect, and whether other predictors also predict STAT3.  I register a STAT3-centered predictor battery because STAT3 now has a moderate independently validated association and is biologically interpretable as a signaling dependency node. PIK3CA mutation among PTEN-wild-type cells tests whether a related PI3K-pathway alteration predicts STAT3 when PTEN is intact; this helps distinguish a PTEN-specific STAT3 association from a broader PI3K/STAT3 axis, while avoiding dependence on possibly rare PTEN/PIK3CA co-alteration cells. TP53-wild-type status is tested because TP53-wild-type is the strongest USP7 predictor and could confound PTEN/STAT3 if correlated with TP53 status. SMARCA4-loss, MSI-high, and KEAP1-loss are tested against STAT3 to see whether the major tumor suppressor or genomic markers are broadly associated with dependency scores or remain specific to their accepted outcomes. MYC amplification, APC mutation, NF1 loss, and SMAD4 loss are added as plausible but not yet tested signaling or genomic predictors; any large positive STAT3 estimate would be a candidate sixth major association, but would require independent validation before acceptance.  I also register PTEN-loss specificity tests against USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN. These are not meant to change the PTEN/STAT3 claim but to ask whether PTEN loss predicts the other leading dependencies. If PTEN loss is null for USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN, that strengthens specificity of the PTEN/STAT3 finding. If it is large for several dependencies, PTEN loss may reflect a broader stress or proliferation-associated dependency phenotype rather than STAT3-specific biology.  These proposals deliberately leave the PTEN/STAT3 robustness battery H95-H103 active and add only focused refinements. record.narrative: Due reassessment H9: MSI-high status versus non-MSI-high status associated with stronger WRN dependency now has independent validation R63. The signed estimate is +0.7896 with independent interval +0.7364 to +0.8429 at the stricter validation-adjusted level, closely matching discovery R9 +0.7899, interval +0.7604 to +0.8193. Because the estimates are already signed to direction -1, this means MSI-high cells have a more negative dependency_WRN score, i.e. stronger WRN dependency, than non-MSI-high cells. The effect is very large relative to the observed distribution of dependency_WRN, whose SD is about 0.263, so this is roughly three SD, and the lower validation bound remains very large. This is concordant with accepted related claims H17, H42, H55, H60, H66, H72, H76, and H89, showing persistence across mutation-burden, library, culture, batch_a, high-quality screens, TP53 contexts, and adenocarcinoma restriction. I therefore reaffirm H9 as accepted and closed as a robust within-dataset association. Synthesis: the currently supported associations are TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. Negative direct-target and pathway tests remain substantial, supporting the interpretation that only a small number of measured genomic predictors are associated with strong dependency differences in this dataset. The main unresolved uncertainties are biological interpretation and external generalizability, especially the counterintuitive KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction and the possibility that accepted predictors are proxies for correlated genomic programs. The next useful analysis remains the direct TP53-stratum estimates for PTEN/STAT3 H116/H117, because H95 suggested possible but imprecise attenuation among TP53-loss cells; this will clarify whether PTEN/STAT3 should be treated as a general within-dataset association or restricted to TP53-intact contexts.

record.narrative: All proposals use the registered signed-direction convention. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency. The main remaining PTEN/STAT3 questions are whether the accepted PTEN-loss effect remains in PIK3CA-wild-type and KRAS-mutant contexts, whether it is STAT3-specific rather than a broader dependency association, and whether the leading accepted predictors show outcome specificity. The PIK3CA-wild-type PTEN-loss test complements the active PIK3CA/STAT3 probe and asks whether a PTEN-associated STAT3 signal persists without concurrent PIK3CA mutation. The KRAS-mutant PTEN-loss test complements the accepted KRAS-wild-type stratum estimate and asks whether RAS-mutant signaling attenuates, coexists with, or remains unrelated to PTEN/STAT3. PTEN-loss tests against MDM2 and NFE2L2 broaden the earlier null specificity checks against KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, and WRN; non-null large estimates would require reinterpreting PTEN loss as a broader dependency predictor. The TP53-wild-type versus SMARCA2/WRN, SMARCA4-loss versus USP7, MSI-high versus SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss versus USP7 tests probe cross-specificity of the accepted predictors. If these are near null, the accepted associations appear narrow and outcome-specific; if any are large, the predictor may mark a broader dependency state or correlated genomic program. The CDKN2A-loss test among TP53-wild-type cells is mechanistic: CDKN2A/p14ARF loss may reduce dependence on the MDM2-p53 axis, so I anticipate weaker MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. I encode that as direction +1, so a positive signed estimate would support weaker MDM2 dependency. The research-marker-D test against STAT3 is a broad constructed-assay probe; it is expected to be null or small but could reveal latent structure if very large. No validation is requested in this explore stage, and no claim is accepted or rejected.

Iteration 8/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
