Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All new estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For the direction -1 CDKN2A-MDM2 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. The key new mechanistic results are H165 and H166. H165 estimates the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 difference among TP53-intact cells with copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5: +0.122 (95% CI +0.073 to +0.171). H166 estimates the same CDKN2A-loss MDM2 difference in all cells with copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5: +0.135 (95% CI +0.091 to +0.179). These are valid, precise, and large relative to MDM2 SD (about 0.54 and 0.59 SD), so I accept them as within-dataset associations and keep them active pending validation. They argue against the idea that low 9p21 copy loss alone fully mimics CDKN2A loss, because CDKN2A-loss still associates with stronger MDM2 dependency within low-9p21 cells. However, CDKN2A loss is enriched for low 9p21 and complete separation from copy-number severity may remain imperfect. H174 is a useful MTAP co-deletion control: among TP53-intact CDKN2A-intact low-9p21 cells, MTAP loss is not meaningfully associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (+0.031, CI -0.028 to +0.090), so I reject that MTAP loss alone explains the CDKN2A-MDM2 signal in this stratum. Outcome specificity also holds: CDKN2A loss is not associated with USP7 (+0.002, CI -0.038 to +0.043) or WRN (-0.007, CI -0.034 to +0.021) dependencies, so I reject H167 and H168. H173 shows the CDKN2A-MDM2 association in the TP53-intact MYC-amplified context is positive (+0.131, CI +0.037 to +0.225), but the exposed cell count is small (57), so I accept it only as supportive context and not as a precise effect estimate. Technical robustness continues to support the major accepted effects: lower screen-quality cells still show strong TP53-intact versus TP53-loss USP7 dependency (+0.797, CI +0.764 to +0.830), SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact SMARCA2 dependency (+0.774, CI +0.743 to +0.804), and MSI-high versus MSI-stable WRN dependency (+0.781, CI +0.730 to +0.832). These are within-dataset associations and not causal or generalizable claims. Null probes reduce concern about overbroad interpretation: marker D with MDM2 is small and not supporting its registered direction (-0.019, CI -0.039 to +0.001); marker E with STAT3 is tiny (+0.015, CI -0.007 to +0.036); PTEN loss with BRAF dependency is tiny and effectively null (+0.023, CI -0.000 to +0.046). I reject these because they are not scientifically meaningful and intervals include or nearly include zero. Multiplicity is controlled by judgment and consistency rather than a single p-value threshold: the CDKN2A-MDM2 results are consistent with prior CDKN2A-MDM2 discovery and validation, while null probes and outcome-specificity checks do not show generic dependency patterns. Because the central residual issue is whether CDKN2A-MDM2 remains in low 9p21 copy-loss cells, I request independent validation for H166, the unstratified low-9p21 CDKN2A-MDM2 comparison.

record.narrative: The strongest remaining scientific question is whether the reproducible CDKN2A-loss/stronger-MDM2-dependency association is a stable CDKN2A-loss marker across TP53 status and copy-number contexts, or whether it is partially localized to low 9p21/MTAP co-loss. I therefore propose TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates both outside the low-9p21 stratum and inside the low-9p21 stratum. These refine the accepted but less precise TP53-loss CDKN2A claim. I also add a MTAP-loss control outside the low-9p21 stratum, complementing the low-9p21 MTAP control and the active overall MTAP test. If CDKN2A remains positive outside low 9p21 and the active low-versus-complement interaction is small, the evidence will support a relatively stable CDKN2A-loss association. If CDKN2A is null outside low 9p21 while MTAP or interaction signals appear, the association is better described as low-9p21/co-deletion localized. For the PTEN-STAT3 association, I test whether the effect remains among PIK3CA-mutant cells and whether PIK3CA status formally modifies the PTEN effect, which is a biologically coherent PI3K/PTEN context check. I also test CDKN2A loss against STAT3 dependency as an outcome-specificity control, because the main CDKN2A effect is on MDM2 and null probes help limit broad overinterpretation. All new estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction; for direction -1, positive signed values correspond to stronger dependency in the exposed group. These are within-dataset associations, not causal or generalizability claims. I closed H171 and H172 because their 9p21 thresholds are essentially non-informative duplicates of overall/TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 comparisons, and closed the low-priority marker-D USP7 probe to allocate analysis slots to the CDKN2A specificity and PTEN/PIK3CA follow-up.

record.narrative:
I am requesting twelve already registered comparisons, all currently without direct evidence, to resolve the central remaining uncertainty about the CDKN2A-loss/MDD2-dependency association and to perform two coherent PIK3CA/PTEN and outcome-specificity checks. The primary set H180-H188 partitions the CDKN2A-MDM2 question by TP53 status, MTAP status, and 9p21 copy-number context. H180 tests CDKN2A loss against MDM2 dependency in the relatively clean triple-restricted setting TP53-intact, MTAP-intact, low 9p21 (copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5), where nearby 9p21 copy loss is forced to be present but MTAP co-loss is excluded. H181 tests a more extreme low-copy stratum (copy_number_9p21 <= -0.75) across the whole population. H182 is the low-9p21 MTAP control in CDKN2A-intact cells: MTAP loss exposed versus MTAP-intact comparator. H183 tests CDKN2A loss outside the low-9p21 stratum (copy_number_9p21 >= -0.5) to see whether the association persists where CDKN2A-loss cells are less likely to be extreme copy-loss cells. H184 formally tests interaction, estimating CDKN2A-loss effect in low-9p21 cells minus the effect in non-low-9p21 cells; a positive signed interaction would indicate greater CDKN2A association in the low-9p21 context, whereas a small interval around zero would support a relatively context-stable CDKN2A-loss association. H185 tests MTAP loss alone in a broader TP53-intact CDKN2A-intact setting, complementing the low-9p21 MTAP controls and assessing whether MTAP co-deletion is independently sufficient. H186 and H187 examine the TP53-loss context by 9p21 copy number, to clarify whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association outside TP53-intact cells is stable, context-dependent, or merely a small and imprecise stratum. H188 tests MTAP in CDKN2A-intact TP53-intact cells but restricted to the non-low-9p21 copy context, giving a final MTAP-specificity control.

The PTEN/PI3K block H189-H190 tests whether the accepted PTEN-loss/stronger-STAT3-dependency association remains among PIK3CA-mutant cells and whether PIK3CA mutation formally modifies the PTEN effect. This is a biologically motivated pathway context check: if PTEN and PIK3CA converge on STAT3 dependency, the PTEN effect might persist in PIK3CA-mutant cells; if PIK3CA mutation largely masks PTEN, the stratum estimate may be smaller. H191 tests CDKN2A loss against STAT3 dependency as an outcome-specificity control, because CDKN2A has a strong MDM2 effect and STAT3 provides a different dependency axis; a null CDKN2A-STAT3 estimate would support specificity rather than a broad dependency pattern.

All requested analyses are interpreted using the existing signed-reporting convention: for direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates support the hypothesis direction, which for continuous dependency scores means more negative dependency in the exposed or exposed-comparator contrast. Direction 1 claims are interpreted directly as the registered positive-direction contrast. For interactions, positive signed values mean the subgroup effect exceeds the complement effect under the registered direction. I will not treat statistically suggestive but tiny intervals as scientifically meaningful unless the estimate is large relative to outcome variance or clearly exceeds the practical importance criterion. Invalid insufficient-cell diagnostics will remain unresolved or closed without evidence rather than converted into claims. These are within-dataset associations only and will not be described as causal or externally generalizable.

Do not claim causality or generalizability beyond dataset.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The strongest remaining scientific question is whether the reproducible CDKN2A-loss/stronger-MDM2-dependency association is a stable CDKN2A-loss marker across TP53 status and copy-number contexts, or whether it is partially localized to low 9p21/MTAP co-loss. I therefore propose TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates both outside the low-9p21 stratum and inside the low-9p21 stratum. These refine the accepted but less precise TP53-loss CDKN2A claim. I also add a MTAP-loss control outside the low-9p21 stratum, complementing the low-9p21 MTAP control and the active overall MTAP test. If CDKN2A remains positive outside low 9p21 and the active low-versus-complement interaction is small, the evidence will support a relatively stable CDKN2A-loss association. If CDKN2A is null outside low 9p21 while MTAP or interaction signals appear, the association is better described as low-9p21/co-deletion localized. For the PTEN-STAT3 association, I test whether the effect remains among PIK3CA-mutant cells and whether PIK3CA status formally modifies the PTEN effect, which is a biologically coherent PI3K/PTEN context check. I also test CDKN2A loss against STAT3 dependency as an outcome-specificity control, because the main CDKN2A effect is on MDM2 and null probes help limit broad overinterpretation. All new estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction; for direction -1, positive signed values correspond to stronger dependency in the exposed group. These are within-dataset associations, not causal or generalizability claims. I closed H171 and H172 because their 9p21 thresholds are essentially non-informative duplicates of overall/TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 comparisons, and closed the low-priority marker-D USP7 probe to allocate analysis slots to the CDKN2A specificity and PTEN/PIK3CA follow-up.","analyze":"I am requesting twelve already registered comparisons, all currently without direct evidence, to resolve the central remaining uncertainty about the CDKN2A-loss/MDD2-dependency association and to perform two coherent PIK3CA/PTEN and outcome-specificity checks. The primary set H180-H188 partitions the CDKN2A-MDM2 question by TP53 status, MTAP status, and 9p21 copy-number context. H180 tests CDKN2A loss against MDM2 dependency in the relatively clean triple-restricted setting TP53-intact, MTAP-intact, low 9p21 (copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5), where nearby 9p21 copy loss is forced to be present but MTAP co-loss is excluded. H181 tests a more extreme low-copy stratum (copy_number_9p21 <= -0.75) across the whole population. H182 is the low-9p21 MTAP control in CDKN2A-intact cells: MTAP loss exposed versus MTAP-intact comparator. H183 tests CDKN2A loss outside the low-9p21 stratum (copy_number_9p21 >= -0.5) to see whether the association persists where CDKN2A-loss cells are less likely to be extreme copy-loss cells. H184 formally tests interaction, estimating CDKN2A-loss effect in low-9p21 cells minus the effect in non-low-9p21 cells; a positive signed interaction would indicate greater CDKN2A association in the low-9p21 context, whereas a small interval around zero would support a relatively context-stable CDKN2A-loss association. H185 tests MTAP loss alone in a broader TP53-intact CDKN2A-intact setting, complementing the low-9p21 MTAP controls and assessing whether MTAP co-deletion is independently sufficient. H186 and H187 examine the TP53-loss context by 9p21 copy number, to clarify whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association outside TP53-intact cells is stable, context-dependent, or merely a small and imprecise stratum. H188 tests MTAP in CDKN2A-intact TP53-intact cells but restricted to the non-low-9p21 copy context, giving a final MTAP-specificity control.\n\nThe PTEN/PI3K block H189-H190 tests whether the accepted PTEN-loss/stronger-STAT3-dependency association remains among PIK3CA-mutant cells and whether PIK3CA mutation formally modifies the PTEN effect. This is a biologically motivated pathway context check: if PTEN and PIK3CA converge on STAT3 dependency, the PTEN effect might persist in PIK3CA-mutant cells; if PIK3CA mutation largely masks PTEN, the stratum estimate may be smaller. H191 tests CDKN2A loss against STAT3 dependency as an outcome-specificity control, because CDKN2A has a strong MDM2 effect and STAT3 provides a different dependency axis; a null CDKN2A-STAT3 estimate would support specificity rather than a broad dependency pattern.\n\nAll requested analyses are interpreted using the existing signed-reporting convention: for direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates support the hypothesis direction, which for continuous dependency scores means more negative dependency in the exposed or exposed-comparator contrast. record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered direction. For the CDKN2A-MDM2 claims with direction -1, positive signed values mean CDKN2A-loss cells have a more negative MDM2 dependency score, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. H180 is the key new mechanistic result: among TP53-intact, MTAP-intact cells restricted to low 9p21 copy number, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (+0.113; 95% CI +0.058 to +0.167; n=231 exposed, 98 comparator). This is about 0.50 SD units and is consistent with the broader validated CDKN2A-MDM2 effect. Because MTAP-intact cells are forced into the stratum, it argues that nearby MTAP co-loss is not necessary to explain the association. This is the most valuable remaining independent validation target, so I request validation for H180. H187, TP53-loss CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-intact MDM2 dependency within low 9p21, gives a larger positive estimate (+0.204; +0.106 to +0.303; n=79 exposed, 23 comparator). It is scientifically meaningful in magnitude and consistent with the broader TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 result, but the comparator count is barely above the threshold, so I accept it only as a supportive within-dataset stratum estimate. H181 is also positive but uses only 29 comparator cells, so I do not convert it into an accepted standalone association; the evidence is suggestive but too sparse for a precise claim. H183 estimates CDKN2A loss outside the low-9p21 stratum and is positive but extremely imprecise (+0.114; -0.043 to +0.272; n=27 exposed, 1457 comparator), leaving whether the effect persists robustly outside low 9p21 unresolved. H184 tests interaction between low-9p21 and non-low-9p21 contexts; the interaction is small and uncertain (+0.020; -0.143 to +0.184), so I reject the registered positive localization hypothesis, while noting that the complement stratum is sparse and this is not proof of exact context equivalence. MTAP controls continue to argue against a generic MTAP explanation: H182 low-9p21 CDKN2A-intact MTAP loss is null (+0.039; -0.020 to +0.098), H185 broad MTAP-alone is tiny (+0.009; -0.015 to +0.033), and H188 non-low-9p21 MTAP-alone is tiny (+0.007; -0.019 to +0.032); I reject these as meaningful associations. Outcome specificity remains supported: CDKN2A loss is not associated with STAT3 dependency (H191, -0.005; -0.032 to +0.021). For PTEN-STAT3, the effect persists among PIK3CA-mutant cells (H189, +0.268; +0.127 to +0.409; n=38 exposed, 305 comparator), supporting pathway robustness despite small exposed count. The PIK3CA status interaction is essentially null and uncertain (H190, +0.001; -0.150 to +0.152), so I reject a registered positive modification claim. H186 is invalid because the TP53-loss non-low-9p21 CDKN2A comparator has only 2 cells, so it remains unresolved and closed. Overall, the CDKN2A-MDM2 conclusion is strengthening: it is not explained by MTAP alone, appears in low-copy 9p21 contexts, and is outcome-specific, while H180 validation will determine whether the MTAP-intact low-9p21 stratum estimate reproduces independently.

H166 tests CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact MDM2 dependency within cells with relatively low 9p21 copy number, copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5. Discovery R143 gave +0.1347 and independent validation R154 gave +0.1096, with a strict validation interval +0.0356 to +0.1836. I accept H166 and close it. H174 and H148 further argue against MTAP loss alone driving the signal, and H167/H168 support outcome specificity because CDKN2A loss does not associate with USP7 or WRN dependency. The central scientific conclusion from this CDKN2A-MDM2 investigation is therefore a reproducible within-dataset association: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, most precisely in TP53-intact and low-9p21 contexts, and this association is not reproduced generically for neighboring dependencies. The broader evidence now supports six major within-dataset dependency associations. Third, MSI-high versus MSI-stable cells have stronger WRN dependency; H9 validated at approximately +0.790, about 3.0 WRN SD units, and MSI-high does not show broad dependency associations for DHX9, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, STAT3, or SMARCA2. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; H13 is accepted after the original negative-direction test rejected because the signed raw direction is positive, with validation approximately +0.802 and lower-quality screen strata similar. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; H94 validated at approximately +0.292, and PTEN loss is not associated with KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, NFE2L2, or many other dependencies, indicating relative specificity. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is now supported by discovery and independent validation for MDM2 dependency overall, in TP53-intact cells, and in low-9p21 cells, with TP53-loss cells also showing a smaller positive association that remains accepted but less precise. Important negative findings are equally informative. Simple driver-gene matching is not supported for KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, or ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency. TP53 loss is not associated with MDM2 dependency in the primary H5 test, and TP53 loss does not explain the STAT3, DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or WRN patterns. MYC amplification is not associated with POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, KIF18A, or STAT3 dependency as a simple effect. PIK3CA, SMAD4, NF1, APC, STK11, RB1, BRCA2, CDKN2A outside MDM2, MTAP alone, and constructed markers D/E do not show broad meaningful dependency associations. These negative results reduce the risk of overgeneralizing the positive associations to the whole dependency panel. Remaining uncertainty is primarily mechanistic and contextual, not evidentiary. The CDKN2A-MDM2 finding remains an association within this dataset, not a causal statement and not an external claim. The next most informative analyses are the newly proposed H183, H184, and H185. H183 directly estimates the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect outside the low-9p21 stratum. H184 formally tests whether the CDKN2A effect differs between low and less low 9p21 copy-number contexts. record.narrative:
All estimates below are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For dependency outcomes with direction -1, a positive signed mean_difference means the exposed cells have a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. I judged practical importance using the effect magnitude relative to the outcome SD and the strict independent-validation interval, rather than a literal 10% relative change on a negative continuous score.  

H154 is the due response deadline for the overall CDKN2A-loss MDM2-dependency claim. Discovery R129 gave a signed estimate +0.1169 [0.0823,0.1516] (n=401 CDKN2A-loss vs 1599 intact). Independent validation R141 gave +0.1141 [0.0668,0.1614] (n=435 vs 1565). The point estimate is about 0.5 MDM2 SD units, and the strict validation interval excludes zero. This is strong within-dataset evidence that CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency than CDKN2A-intact cells across the population. I accept H154 and close it.  

H180 is the new validation result for the highly restricted context TP53-intact, MTAP-intact, low 9p21 copy number (copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5). Discovery R155 gave +0.1126 [0.0578,0.1674] (n=231 vs 98). Independent validation R166 gave +0.0848 [0.0037,0.1660] (n=245 vs 83). The validation is positive and its strict interval barely excludes zero, but it is attenuated and imprecise because the comparator has only 83 cells. Scientifically, this supports the key point that the CDKN2A-MDM2 association can persist when nearby MTAP co-loss is excluded within TP53-intact low-copy 9p21 cells. However, the lower confidence bound near zero means the magnitude in this exact stratum is uncertain. I accept H180 as a validated but imprecise stratum association and close the original claim.  

Final synthesis: the dataset supports six major within-dataset dependency associations. TP53 wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells (H6 validated around +0.81, about 2.2 USP7 SD). SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells (H7 validated around +0.80, about 2.2 SMARCA2 SD), and ARID1A loss does not show the same effect. MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency than MSI-stable cells (H9 validated around +0.79, about 3.0 WRN SD). KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact cells (H13 validated around +0.80; positive signed direction corresponds to less negative NFE2L2 scores). PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells (H94 validated around +0.29, about 1.2 STAT3 SD). CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency than CDKN2A-intact cells (H154 validated around +0.11, about 0.5 MDM2 SD), with robust support also in TP53-intact and low-9p21 contexts and, cautiously, in TP53-intact/MTAP-intact/low-9p21 cells.  

The CDKN2A-MDM2 finding is especially strengthened by context and specificity checks. It is not explained by MTAP loss alone: MTAP-alone effects were null or tiny, including MTAP-intact low-9p21 CDKN2A tests and broader MTAP-alone tests. It is outcome-specific: CDKN2A loss was not associated with USP7, WRN, STAT3, or many other dependencies. The low-9p21 interaction test H184 was small and uncertain, so I did not support a strong localization claim, but that comparison was sparse. H183 remains unresolved because CDKN2A-loss cells outside low 9p21 are too few, leaving open how far the CDKN2A-MDM2 association extends beyond the low-copy context. H187 supports CDKN2A loss in TP53-loss low-9p21 cells, but its comparator is sparse and should be treated as supportive rather than precise.  

Important negative findings are also informative. Simple driver-gene matching is not supported: KRAS mutation is not associated with stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E is not associated with stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification is not associated with stronger EGFR dependency; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency. TP53 loss is not associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in the primary H5 test and is not a broad driver of STAT3, DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or WRN effects. MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, PIK3CA status as an effect modifier for PTEN-STAT3, STK11 loss, RB1 loss, BRCA2 loss, APC, SMAD4, NF1, MTAP alone, and several constructed marker assays are either null or unsupported as broad dependency predictors. PTEN loss is also relatively specific: it is not associated with KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, or NFE2L2 dependency in the major tests.  

Remaining uncertainty is mostly contextual and precision-related, not evidentiary for the headline effects. The PTEN-STAT3 batch-A stratum remains unresolved after validation because the validation interval crossed zero, though the main and several subgroup estimates were robust. Several screen/library interactions remain deferred or unresolved because of sparse cells. The CDKN2A-MDM2 effect remains an association, not a causal statement, and should not be described as externally generalizable or biologically explained solely by a named pathway without external evidence.  

The most informative next analysis I registered is a new discovery test of CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact, MTAP-intact cells across all copy-number contexts. This asks whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is a stable marker when MTAP co-loss is excluded without forcing low 9p21. If positive, it further supports MTAP-independent CDKN2A-loss biology; if null, the accepted findings are better interpreted as concentrated in low-copy 9p21/co-deletion contexts. No causal or generalizability claims are made.

I am selecting the twelve currently registered unresolved active comparisons, H193-H204, because they directly extend the established within-dataset associations through specificity, conditional independence, and effect-heterogeneity checks rather than adding redundant estimates of already validated effects. First, H193 and H194 test whether the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association is outcome-specific. The prior evidence showed that PTEN loss was not associated with dependency_KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, or NFE2L2. If PTEN loss is also null for EGFR and KIF18A, this supports selective PTEN/STAT3 biology; if positive, it would indicate a broader PTEN-loss dependency phenotype. Second, H195 and H196 test whether the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association is specific against SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 dependency, while H197 tests whether KEAP1 loss is specific against SMARCA2 dependency. A null result would further support that MTAP co-deletion does not generically drive dependency differences and does not explain the CDKN2A/MDM2 association. Fourth, H199 tests CDKN2A loss against MDM2 dependency among TP53-loss and MTAP-intact cells. This is an important context test: a positive signed estimate would extend the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association beyond TP53-intact cells and without restricting to low 9p21 copy number, whereas a null or underpowered result would keep the association narrower or unresolved. Fifth, H200 tests ARID1A loss against SMARCA2 dependency conditional on SMARCA4-intact cells. Since the accepted SWI/SNF-related effect is SMARCA4 loss, a null ARID1A result supports specificity of the accepted effect; a positive residual effect would suggest broader SWI/SNF complex effects. Sixth, H201 is a constructed-marker negative control: marker F has no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role, so a null association with MDM2 dependency supports assay negative-control behavior, while a large unexpected effect would require caution about constructed-marker artifacts. Finally, H202-H204 are pre-specified high-versus-complement interaction tests using constructed research signatures. These ask whether the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2, PTEN-STAT3, and MSI-WRN associations differ in cells above versus below the registered high-signature threshold. Near-zero interactions would support stability across these constructed orthogonal axes; positive signed interactions under direction -1 would indicate stronger effects in the high-signature subgroup, i.e. effect heterogeneity rather than broad equivalence. All interpretations remain signed to the registered directions: for direction -1 mean_difference, positive estimates indicate stronger dependency in exposed cells relative to comparator cells; for interactions under direction -1, positive estimates indicate a stronger exposed-comparator effect in the subgroup than in its complement. Some interaction tests may fail the minimum cell-count rule, in which case they should remain unresolved or closed without evidence rather than interpreted as null. record.narrative: No validation was requested because the remaining voluntary validation budget is zero. All reported estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 mean differences, positive signed estimates mean that exposed cells have more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction -1 interactions, positive signed estimates mean that the exposed-comparator effect is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. H193 and H194 are specificity controls for the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency effect. PTEN loss was not associated with clinically meaningful differences in EGFR or KIF18A dependency: R167 gave a very small positive estimate (+0.0059; 95% CI -0.0171 to +0.0288) and R168 gave a small negative estimate (-0.0192; -0.0434 to +0.0051). I reject both as unsupported evidence of broader PTEN-loss dependency phenotypes. H195 and H196 test whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association generalizes to other dependency axes. R169 was near zero for SMARCA2 dependency (+0.0089; -0.0319 to +0.0496), and R170 was small and not statistically supported for NFE2L2 dependency (+0.0319; -0.0074 to +0.0711), corresponding to only about 0.09 NFE2L2 SD for the point estimate. I reject both, supporting outcome specificity of CDKN2A loss for MDM2 dependency. H197 tests KEAP1-loss specificity and is near null for SMARCA2 dependency (-0.0059; -0.0463 to +0.0345), so the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding is not part of a broad SMARCA2-dependency phenotype. H198 tests MTAP loss on WRN dependency among TP53-intact, CDKN2A-intact cells; the estimate is tiny and null (-0.0096; -0.0477 to +0.0284), further supporting that MTAP alone does not explain the strong dependency associations, especially the CDKN2A-MDM2 signal. H199 is the only new main accepted result. Among TP53-loss, MTAP-intact cells, CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (+0.0998; 95% CI +0.0182 to +0.1815; n=69 exposed vs 264 comparator). This is about 0.44 MDM2 SD, a scientifically meaningful magnitude relative to the outcome distribution, and the 95% interval excludes zero. It extends the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association beyond TP53-intact and low-copy contexts and beyond MTAP co-loss, while remaining a within-dataset association and not a causal claim. H200 tests ARID1A loss conditional on SMARCA4-intact cells for SMARCA2 dependency; the result is null (-0.0031; -0.0252 to +0.0190), supporting specificity of the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2-dependency effect rather than a broad SWI/SNF-complex effect. H201 is a constructed-marker negative control; marker F positive cells showed no meaningful MDM2 dependency difference (+0.0129; -0.0069 to +0.0328), which is reassuring for specificity and against a generic assay artifact. H202 tests whether CDKN2A-MDM2 is modified by high research_signature A. The signed interaction is positive but statistically uncertain (+0.0679; -0.0139 to +0.1497), so I reject the registered positive modification claim; the data do not support signature-A heterogeneity for CDKN2A-MDM2. H204 tests whether MSI-WRN is modified by high research_signature C; the signed interaction is negative and uncertain (-0.0428; -0.1046 to +0.0191), so I reject the registered positive heterogeneity claim and see no evidence that this signature split changes the stable MSI-WRN association. H203 produced a large negative signed interaction for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in cells with high research_signature B (-0.4105; 95% CI -0.4881 to -0.3330). Under the registered direction -1, positive signed interaction was the hypothesis; the observed direction is opposite. I reject the original H203 claim. However, because research_signature B is a constructed arbitrary-unit assay and this is a single strong interaction among many tests, I do not promote the opposite direction to a final accepted biological conclusion yet. I registered a reversed interaction and a direct high-signature-B mean-difference probe to determine whether the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association is attenuated, absent, or reversed in that subgroup. Overall, H193-H204 sharpen specificity of the main accepted associations: PTEN-loss/STAT3 appears STAT3-specific, CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 appears MDM2-specific and MTAP-independent across contexts, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 is outcome-specific, MTAP-alone and marker-F controls remain null, and constructed-signature effect modification is mostly unsupported except for an unexpected signature-B interaction that requires follow-up but should not be overinterpreted.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

The prior evidence showed that PTEN loss was not associated with dependency_KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, or NFE2L2. If PTEN loss is also null for EGFR and KIF18A, this supports selective PTEN/STAT3 biology; if positive, it would indicate a broader PTEN-loss dependency phenotype. Second, H195 and H196 test whether the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association is specific against SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 dependency, while H197 tests whether KEAP1 loss is specific against SMARCA2 dependency. These are outcome-specificity controls for two of the strongest accepted effects. Third, H198 tests MTAP loss against WRN dependency among TP53-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells. A null result would further support that MTAP co-deletion does not generically drive dependency differences and does not explain the CDKN2A/MDM2 association. Fourth, H199 tests CDKN2A loss against MDM2 dependency among TP53-loss and MTAP-intact cells. This is an important context test: a positive signed estimate would extend the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association beyond TP53-intact cells and without restricting to low 9p21 copy number, whereas a null or underpowered result would keep the association narrower or unresolved. Fifth, H200 tests ARID1A loss against SMARCA2 dependency conditional on SMARCA4-intact cells. Since the accepted SWI/SNF-related effect is SMARCA4 loss, a null ARID1A result supports specificity of the accepted effect; a positive residual effect would suggest broader SWI/SNF complex effects. Sixth, H201 is a constructed-marker negative control: marker F has no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role, so a null association with MDM2 dependency supports assay negative-control behavior, while a large unexpected effect would require caution about constructed-marker artifacts. Finally, H202-H204 are pre-specified high-versus-complement interaction tests using constructed research signatures. These ask whether the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2, PTEN-STAT3, and MSI-WRN associations differ in cells above versus below the registered high-signature threshold. Near-zero interactions would support stability across these constructed orthogonal axes; positive signed interactions under direction -1 would indicate stronger effects in the high-signature subgroup, i.e. effect heterogeneity rather than broad equivalence. All interpretations remain signed to the registered directions: for direction -1 mean_difference, positive estimates indicate stronger dependency in exposed cells relative to comparator cells; for interactions under direction -1, positive estimates indicate a stronger exposed-comparator effect in the subgroup than in its complement. record.narrative:
I assess the due validation of H166. Under direction -1, positive signed estimates mean that exposed cells have a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. H166 tests CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-intact MDM2 dependency within cells with low 9p21 copy number, copy_number_9p21 <= -0.5. Discovery R143 gave a signed estimate +0.1347 [0.0907, 0.1786] in 374 CDKN2A-loss versus 142 intact cells, and independent validation R154 gave +0.1096 [0.0356, 0.1836] in 395 versus 109 cells. The validation estimate is about 0.5 MDM2 SD and its strict interval excludes zero. I accept H166 and close the investigation as a supported within-dataset association: CDKN2A-loss cells show stronger MDM2 dependency than CDKN2A-intact cells in the low-9p21 subgroup. I do not interpret the copy-number threshold as causal mechanism, because CDKN2A loss is closely tied to local 9p21 copy number and this remains an association in this supplied dataset only.

Final scientific synthesis. For continuous dependency scores with negative values, the 10% relative threshold is not directly meaningful, so I judged importance by effect magnitude relative to outcome SD and by strict validation intervals. The dataset now supports six principal dependency associations. First, TP53 wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells, with validated effect around +0.81, about 2.2 USP7 SD. Second, SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells, validated around +0.80, about 2.2 SMARCA2 SD; ARID1A loss does not show the same effect. Third, MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency than MSI-stable cells, validated around +0.79, about 3.0 WRN SD. Fourth, KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact cells; the positive signed estimate for the reversed claim corresponds to less negative NFE2L2 scores, about +0.80. Fifth, PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells, validated around +0.29, about 1.2 STAT3 SD, and this effect is STAT3-specific across many null dependency axes. Sixth, CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency than CDKN2A-intact cells, overall validated around +0.114, and the effect is supported in several contexts: TP53-intact cells, TP53-loss MTAP-intact cells, low-9p21 cells overall and TP53-intact, and now H166 validates the low-9p21 overall subgroup. The CDKN2A-MDM2 association appears MDM2-specific and largely MTAP-independent: MTAP-alone effects were null or small, and CDKN2A loss was null for USP7, WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2.

Important negative findings sharpen the biology and reduce naive interpretations. Driver-gene matching is not supported: KRAS mutation does not predict stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E does not predict stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification does not predict stronger EGFR dependency; ERBB2 amplification does not predict stronger ERBB2 dependency. TP53 loss is not associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in the primary test and is not a broad driver of STAT3, DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or WRN effects. MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, RB1 loss, BRCA2 loss, APC, SMAD4, NF1, and several constructed marker assays are null or unsupported as broad dependency predictors. PTEN loss does not broadly predict EGFR, KIF18A, KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, NFE2L2, or BRAF dependency. These negative controls make the accepted associations more selective and reduce the likelihood that a single confounded population split explains them. However, all remain associations within this supplied dataset; they are not causal statements and may not generalize to other cohorts, lineages, screen libraries, or biological settings.

Unresolved uncertainty is now mostly contextual rather than evidentiary for headline effects. The PTEN-STAT3 batch-A stratum remains unresolved because its validation interval crossed zero, even though the main PTEN-STAT3 effect was robust. Several screen-library and batch interactions remain deferred or unresolved because of sparse cells. The CDKN2A-MDM2 association outside low 9p21 is difficult to test because CDKN2A-loss cells are sparse outside low-copy 9p21, leaving H183 unresolved; H181 and H187 are supportive but sparse. The largest recent unresolved issue is the unexpected research_signature B interaction for PTEN-STAT3. The original H203 was registered with a positive signed heterogeneity hypothesis but produced a large opposite-signed interaction; the reversed follow-up H205 is strong but was registered after inspection and cannot be externally validated because validation budget is exhausted. I therefore keep the signature-B modification unresolved rather than promoting it to a headline finding. It could represent real context dependence of PTEN-STAT3, an arbitrary constructed-signature artifact, or a multiple-comparison pattern. Clarifying it internally is the most informative next analysis.

Next investigation. I keep H205 and H206 active: reversed signature-B interaction and direct high-signature-B PTEN-STAT3 mean difference. I also registered a new complementary low-signature-B test, PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 dependency within research_signature_b <= 0.5. Together these analyses will determine whether the PTEN-STAT3 association is robust below the signature-B threshold, attenuated or reversed above it, or whether the apparent interaction is unstable. Since no voluntary validation budget remains, these are discovery-stage within-dataset checks. The accepted scientific conclusions remain: selective, strong within-dataset associations of TP53 status with USP7, SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2, MSI-high with WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2, PTEN loss with STAT3, and CDKN2A loss with MDM2, with the low-9p21 CDKN2A-MDM2 stratum now independently validated.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and no independent validation can be requested because the validation budget is exhausted. The most valuable next comparisons are focused within-dataset tests that resolve the unexpected research_signature_B PTEN/STAT3 finding while asking whether research_signature_B is a generic modifier of the other strong accepted associations or a PTEN/STAT3-specific context. I registered four PTEN/STAT3 signature-B stratum tests. The extreme-high test (signature_B >= 1) uses direction +1 to test the working hypothesis that PTEN-loss cells show attenuation or reversal of the accepted stronger STAT3 dependency in that stratum: a positive signed mean estimate would mean PTEN-loss cells have less negative, or weaker, STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells. The middle-band test (-0.5 <= signature_B <= 0.5) and extreme-low test (signature_B <= -1) use direction -1 so that a positive signed estimate means the accepted PTEN-loss/stronger-STAT3-dependency pattern is preserved: PTEN-loss cells have more negative STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells. The extreme-high interaction also uses direction +1; a positive signed interaction would mean that the PTEN-loss effect in signature_B >= 1 is more positive, hence attenuated or reversed, relative to the complement, whereas a negative signed interaction would mean it is stronger in that extreme-high stratum. I also registered signature_B interaction controls for the other principal accepted associations: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-status/USP7, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, MSI-high/WRN, and CDKN2A-loss/MDM2. These interaction directions are chosen to align with the accepted raw contrasts for those effects, so for a near-zero interaction there is little evidence of signature-B modification. For direction -1 accepted-effect controls, a positive signed interaction would mean the accepted effect is stronger in high signature_B than in its complement, whereas a negative signed interaction would mean attenuation in high signature_B. For KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, the accepted raw contrast is positive because KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, so direction +1 aligns with the accepted effect. These tests distinguish several alternatives: if only PTEN/STAT3 changes across signature_B, signature_B may mark a PTEN/STAT3-specific constructed context or interaction artifact; if several accepted effects are modified, signature_B may be a broad technical or population modifier; if signature_B interactions are near zero and PTEN/STAT3 middle and low strata preserve the accepted effect, the original reversed signature-B interaction is more likely an isolated constructed-signature interaction rather than a general biological effect modifier. Second, SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells, validated around +0.80, about 2.2 SMARCA2 SD; ARID1A loss does not show the same effect. Third, MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency than MSI-stable cells, validated around +0.79, about 3.0 WRN SD. Fourth, KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact cells; the positive signed estimate for the reversed claim corresponds to less negative NFE2L2 scores, about +0.80. Fifth, PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells, validated around +0.29, about 1.2 STAT3 SD, and this effect is STAT3-specific across many null dependency axes. Sixth, CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency than CDKN2A-intact cells, overall validated around +0.114, and the effect is supported in several contexts: TP53-intact cells, TP53-loss MTAP-intact cells, low-9p21 cells overall and TP53-intact, and now H166 validates the low-9p21 overall subgroup. The CDKN2A-MDM2 association appears MDM2-specific and largely MTAP-independent: MTAP-alone effects were null or small, and CDKN2A loss was null for USP7, WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2.\n\nImportant negative findings sharpen the biology and reduce naive interpretations. Driver-gene matching is not supported: KRAS mutation does not predict stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E does not predict stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification does not predict stronger EGFR dependency; ERBB2 amplification does not predict stronger ERBB2 dependency. TP53 loss is not associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in the primary test and is not a broad driver of STAT3, DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or WRN effects. MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, RB1 loss, BRCA2 loss, APC, SMAD4, NF1, and several constructed marker assays are null or unsupported as broad dependency predictors. PTEN loss does not broadly predict EGFR, KIF18A, KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, NFE2L2, or BRAF dependency. These negative controls make the accepted associations more selective and reduce the likelihood that a single confounded population split explains them. However, all remain associations within this supplied dataset; they are not causal statements and may not generalize to other cohorts, lineages, screen libraries, or biological settings.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty is now mostly contextual rather than evidentiary for headline effects. The PTEN-STAT3 batch-A stratum remains unresolved because its validation interval crossed zero, even though the main PTEN-STAT3 effect was robust. Several screen-library and batch interactions remain deferred or unresolved because of sparse cells. The CDKN2A-MDM2 association outside low 9p21 is difficult to test because CDKN2A-loss cells are sparse outside low-copy 9p21, leaving H183 unresolved; H181 and H187 are supportive but sparse. The largest recent unresolved issue is the unexpected research_signature B interaction for PTEN-STAT3. The original H203 was registered with a positive signed heterogeneity hypothesis but produced a large opposite-signed interaction; the reversed follow-up H205 is strong but was registered after inspection and cannot be externally validated because validation budget is exhausted. I therefore keep the signature-B modification unresolved rather than promoting it to a headline finding. It could represent real context dependence of PTEN-STAT3, an arbitrary constructed-signature artifact, or a multiple-comparison pattern. Clarifying it internally is the most informative next analysis.\n\nNext investigation. I keep H205 and H206 active: reversed signature-B interaction and direct high-signature-B PTEN-STAT3 mean difference. I also registered a new complementary low-signature-B test, PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 dependency within research_signature_b <= 0.5. Together these analyses will determine whether the PTEN-STAT3 association is robust below the signature-B threshold, attenuated or reversed above it, or whether the apparent interaction is unstable. Since no voluntary validation budget remains, these are discovery-stage within-dataset checks. The accepted scientific conclusions remain: selective, strong within-dataset associations of TP53 status with USP7, SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2, MSI-high with WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2, PTEN loss with STAT3, and CDKN2A loss with MDM2, with the low-9p21 CDKN2A-MDM2 stratum now independently validated."}}

record.narrative:
No validation was requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. All estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction. For direction -1 mean contrasts, positive signed estimates mean the exposed group has more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction -1 interactions, positive signed estimates mean the exposed-comparator effect is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. For direction +1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive, i.e. higher/less negative dependency scores for the exposed group, or a more positive raw interaction for direction +1 interactions.

The PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency pattern is now much clearer. The accepted overall PTEN-loss effect is preserved in cells with research_signature_b <= 0.5: H207 (<=0.5) gives +0.392 [0.327, 0.457], H209 (-0.5 to 0.5) gives +0.367 [0.278, 0.456], and H210 (<= -1) gives +0.387 [0.256, 0.517]. These are roughly 1.5-1.6 STAT3 SD and intervals exclude zero, so I accept them. In high research_signature_b, direct mean differences are not statistically meaningful: H206 (>=0.5) gives +0.018 [-0.025, 0.061] and H208 (>=1) gives +0.021 [-0.041, 0.083]. Because direction is +1, these positive point estimates would correspond to weaker STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells, but their magnitudes are tiny (<0.1 STAT3 SD) and intervals cross zero. I therefore reject H206 and H208 as claims of a meaningful positive direct high-signature-B difference. They are, however, consistent with an attenuated or nearly absent PTEN effect in high signature B rather than a strong reversal.

The interaction results support that context dependence. H211, pre-registered specifically for the extreme-high stratum research_signature_b >= 1, gives +0.338 [0.254, 0.422] (about 1.4 STAT3 SD), indicating that the raw PTEN-loss effect in high signature B is much more positive, hence attenuated or absent, relative to the complement. I accept H211 and close it. H205 is the broader high-signature-B interaction (>=0.5), +0.411 [0.333, 0.488]. It was originally registered post hoc after H203 gave the opposite direction, but the new pre-registered H211 and the direct stratum results strongly corroborate the same interpretation: PTEN-loss strengthens STAT3 dependency in lower signature-B strata but this association is attenuated toward zero in high signature B. I therefore accept H205 as a within-dataset context association, while keeping it active because research_signature_b is an artificial constructed assay and no independent validation remains.

The control interactions test whether research_signature_b is a generic modifier. H212 (SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2) is near null (+0.025 [-0.016, 0.067]); H214 (KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2) is near null (+0.026 [-0.015, 0.068]); H215 (MSI-high/WRN) is essentially null (-0.006 [-0.068, 0.055]). I reject the registered positive modification claims for H212, H214, and H215. H213 (TP53-status/USP7) shows a statistically supported opposite-signed result: signed estimate -0.058 [-0.102, -0.014]. Under direction -1, this means the accepted USP7 effect is modestly attenuated in high signature B relative to its complement. However, the magnitude is only about 0.16 USP7 SD and it is an opposite-signed result among multiple controls; I do not promote it as a meaningful context effect and reject H213 as registered. Overall, research_signature_b is not a generic modifier of the accepted dependency associations, but it is selectively associated with modification of PTEN/STAT3 and CDKN2A/MDM2 in this dataset.

The strongest new effect-modification result is H216: CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 interaction in high research_signature_b gives +0.195 [0.116, 0.274]. Under direction -1, this means the CDKN2A-loss effect is much stronger in cells with research_signature_b >= 0.5 than in its complement. The interval excludes zero and the interaction is about 0.86 MDM2 SD, which is scientifically meaningful relative to the MDM2 outcome distribution. Because the exposure and subgroup are both pre-registered and the result is strong, I accept H216 as a within-dataset association. I keep it active because research_signature_b is an arbitrary constructed signature, the effect could be a synthetic-context artifact, and direct high/low stratum and confounder-stratified analyses are needed to estimate raw effect sizes and check dependence on TP53 status, MTAP/9p21 co-deletion contexts, or other correlated variables. No validation budget remains, so acceptance here is explicitly a discovery-stage within-dataset conclusion, not a causal or generalizable claim.

The proposed follow-ups are therefore focused on H216 and the PTEN/STAT3 signature-B context: direct CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates in high and low signature B, an extreme-high signature-B interaction, and high-signature-B estimates restricted to TP53-intact or low-9p21 contexts to see whether the modification survives in known mechanistic strata. Marker-D interaction controls for CDKN2A/MDM2 and PTEN/STAT3 test whether the apparent modification is signature-B-specific or a more generic arbitrary-marker artifact.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.
