record.narrative:
I assess the due validation response for H180. Under direction -1, positive signed estimates mean that exposed CDKN2A-loss cells have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. H180 tests CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact among TP53-intact, MTAP-intact, low-9p21 cells. Discovery R155 gave a signed effect of +0.1126 [0.0578,0.1674] in 231 versus 98 cells, and independent validation R166 gave +0.0848 [0.0037,0.1659] in 245 versus 83 cells. The strict validation interval excludes zero and the point estimate is roughly 0.37 MDM2 SD and about 31% of the absolute mean MDM2 score, so the direction and practical magnitude are supported, although the lower validation bound is below the 10% relative benchmark because this nested stratum is small. I accept H180 as a supported within-dataset association and keep it closed; the precise magnitude in this sparse low-9p21 TP53/MTAP-intact stratum remains less certain than the broader CDKN2A-MDM2 association.

Final synthesis. Because dependency scores are negative-valued continuous quantities, I judged scientific meaningfulness primarily against outcome SDs and secondary relative-magnitude benchmarks. All claims are associations in the supplied dataset only. They are not causal statements, not claims that the measured predictor drives dependency, and not guaranteed to generalize beyond this cohort, lineage, culture, library, batch, or screen-quality distribution.

The strongest and most consistently validated associations are selective dependencies rather than broad population effects. First, TP53 non-loss is associated with stronger USP7 dependency: H6 gave validated +0.811 [0.782,0.841], about 2.2 USP7 SD, and the effect is reproduced across library, batch, culture, QC, aneuploidy, and other strata. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H7 gave validated +0.805 [0.774,0.836], about 2.2 SMARCA2 SD, and the pattern is not explained by ARID1A loss. Third, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency: H9 gave validated +0.790 [0.736,0.843], about 3.0 WRN SD, and this is reproduced in TP53, library, batch, QC, mutation-burden, and BRCA2-restricted strata. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H13 gave validated +0.802 [0.775,0.829] in the registered positive direction, about 2.2 NFE2L2 SD. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H94 gave validated +0.292 [0.213,0.370], about 1.2 STAT3 SD, and this effect is STAT3-selective across many other dependency axes; batch-A stratum remains unresolved, but the main effect is robust. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: overall H154 gave validated +0.114 [0.067,0.161]; TP53-intact cells H142 gave validated +0.159 [0.101,0.218]; low-9p21 cells H166 gave validated +0.110 [0.036,0.184]; and H180 now validates the low-9p21 TP53/MTAP-intact subgroup in the same direction. CDKN2A-MDM2 is not a broad dependency effect: CDKN2A loss is null for USP7, WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2, while MTAP-alone effects are weak or null and interaction tests do not strongly support MTAP dependence.

The negative findings are scientifically important because they reduce simple driver-gene matching and broad confounding explanations. KRAS mutation does not predict stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E does not predict stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification does not predict stronger EGFR dependency; ERBB2 amplification does not predict stronger ERBB2 dependency. TP53 loss is not associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in the primary test and is not a broad driver of STAT3, DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or WRN effects. PIK3CA, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, RB1 loss, BRCA2 loss, APC, SMAD4, NF1, and most constructed marker effects are null or unsupported as broad predictors. PTEN loss does not broadly predict EGFR, KIF18A, KRAS, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, MDM2, TMED10, POLR2A, RPL11, NFE2L2, or BRAF dependency. These negative specificity tests make the accepted associations more selective.

The main unresolved layer is context dependence involving research_signature_b. For PTEN/STAT3, the accepted stronger PTEN-loss effect is preserved in low and middle signature-B strata: H207 +0.392 [0.327,0.457], H209 +0.367 [0.278,0.456], H210 +0.387 [0.256,0.517]. In high signature-B strata, direct mean differences H206 and H208 are near zero and not supported as meaningful direct positive differences, while interactions H205 +0.411 [0.333,0.488] and H211 +0.338 [0.254,0.422] support attenuation toward zero. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

For direction +1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive, i.e. higher/less negative dependency scores for the exposed group, or a more positive raw interaction for direction +1 interactions.\n\nThe PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency pattern is now much clearer. The accepted overall PTEN-loss effect is preserved in cells with research_signature_b <= 0.5: H207 (<=0.5) gives +0.392 [0.327, 0.457], H209 (-0.5 to 0.5) gives +0.367 [0.278, 0.456], and H210 (<= -1) gives +0.387 [0.256, 0.517]. These are roughly 1.5-1.6 STAT3 SD and intervals exclude zero, so I accept them. In high research_signature_b, direct mean differences are not statistically meaningful: H206 (>=0.5) gives +0.018 [-0.025, 0.061] and H208 (>=1) gives +0.021 [-0.041, 0.083]. Because direction is +1, these positive point estimates would correspond to weaker STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells, but their magnitudes are tiny (<0.1 STAT3 SD) and intervals cross zero. I therefore reject H206 and H208 as claims of a meaningful positive direct high-signature-B difference. They are, however, consistent with an attenuated or nearly absent PTEN effect in high signature B rather than a strong reversal.\n\nThe interaction results support that context dependence. H211, pre-registered specifically for the extreme-high stratum research_signature_b >= 1, gives +0.338 [0.254, 0.422] (about 1.4 STAT3 SD), indicating that the raw PTEN-loss effect in high signature B is much more positive, hence attenuated or absent, relative to the complement. I accept H211 and close it. H205 is the broader high-signature-B interaction (>=0.5), +0.411 [0.333, 0.488]. It was originally registered post hoc after H203 gave the opposite direction, but the new pre-registered H211 and the direct stratum results strongly corroborate the same interpretation: PTEN-loss strengthens STAT3 dependency in lower signature-B strata but this association is attenuated toward zero in high signature B. I therefore accept H205 as a within-dataset context association, while keeping it active because research_signature_b is an artificial constructed assay and no independent validation remains.\n\nThe control interactions test whether research_signature_b is a generic modifier. H212 (SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2) is near null (+0.025 [-0.016, 0.067]); H214 (KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2) is near null (+0.026 [-0.015, 0.068]); H215 (MSI-high/WRN) is essentially null (-0.006 [-0.068, 0.055]). I reject the registered positive modification claims for H212, H214, and H215. H213 (TP53-status/USP7) shows a statistically supported opposite-signed result: signed estimate -0.058 [-0.102, -0.014]. Under direction -1, this means the accepted USP7 effect is modestly attenuated in high signature B relative to its complement. However, the magnitude is only about 0.16 USP7 SD and it is an opposite-signed result among multiple controls; I do not promote it as a meaningful context effect and reject H213 as registered. Overall, research_signature_b is not a generic modifier of the accepted dependency associations, but it is selectively associated with modification of PTEN/STAT3 and CDKN2A/MDM2 in this dataset.\n\nThe strongest new effect-modification result is H216: CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 interaction in high research_signature_b gives +0.195 [0.116, 0.274]. Under direction -1, this means the CDKN2A-loss effect is much stronger in cells with research_signature_b >= 0.5 than in its complement. The interval excludes zero and the interaction is about 0.86 MDM2 SD, which is scientifically meaningful relative to the MDM2 outcome distribution. record.narrative:
No independent validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator negative difference, i.e. more negative dependency scores in the exposed group and therefore stronger dependency. For direction -1 interactions, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-comparator effect is more negative/stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. For direction +1 interactions, a positive signed estimate means the raw interaction is more positive relative to the complement, which for the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 pattern indicates attenuation toward zero.

The new direct stratum analyses strongly support the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association inside high research_signature_b contexts. H217 gives a signed direct effect of +0.2497 [0.1794, 0.3200] in cells with research_signature_b >= 0.5, which is about 1.1 MDM2 SD and much larger than the nominal benchmark. I accept and close H217. H218 gives a smaller but statistically supported effect in research_signature_b <= 0.5, +0.0547 [0.0177, 0.0916], about 0.24 MDM2 SD. Its lower confidence bound is close to zero, but it is direction-consistent and plausibly above a 10% absolute-mean scale difference; I accept it as a modest direct effect and close it. H220 (+0.2491 [0.1721, 0.3262] within TP53-intact high-signature_b cells), H221 (+0.2745 [0.1886, 0.3604] within low copy_number_9p21 high-signature_b cells), and H225 (+0.2577 [0.1782, 0.3372] within MTAP-intact high-signature_b cells) are large, robust, and support the high-signature_b CDKN2A-MDM2 association without invoking TP53 loss, low 9p21 context, or MTAP status. I accept and close those direct robustness strata.

The specificity controls are mostly reassuring. H222 tests CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 interaction in research_marker_d-positive cells and is null: -0.0219 [-0.0912, 0.0475]. H234 tests the analogous marker-E interaction and is essentially null: -0.00046 [-0.0699, 0.0690]. H223 tests PTEN-loss/STAT3 interaction in marker-D-positive cells and is null: +0.0170 [-0.0877, 0.1218]. H232 and H233 test whether high-signature_b CDKN2A loss spuriously modifies USP7 or STAT3 dependencies; both are near null (+0.0040 [-0.0666, 0.0746] and -0.0211 [-0.0537, 0.0114], respectively). I reject these registered direction-specific interaction or direct-effect claims. They do not support arbitrary marker mimicry of the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 and PTEN-STAT3 associations, and they support MDM2/STAT3 dependency-axis selectivity.

The main caution is that research_signature_b is not uniquely associated with context modification. H236 tests CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 interaction in research_signature_c >= 0.5 and is strongly positive under the registered direction: +0.3880 [0.2996, 0.4764], i.e. the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is much stronger in signature_c-positive cells than in their complement. This is evidence that another constructed signature can mimic the signature_b context pattern. I accept H236 as a within-dataset association, but I keep it active and interpret it as a warning that the signature_b modification may be a constructed-assay/context artifact rather than a biologically specific modifier. H237 similarly tests PTEN-loss/STAT3 interaction in research_signature_a >= 0.5 and is strongly positive under its registered direction: +0.4892 [0.3855, 0.5930], indicating a strong context-dependent modification of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association by another constructed signature. I accept H237 as a within-dataset association and keep it active, but do not promote it as biologically meaningful without validation. I registered direct stratum analyses for signature_c and signature_a to estimate raw high- and lower-signature effects, because interaction estimates alone cannot show whether the mimicking signature has a large raw exposed-comparator effect or mainly reflects a contrast with its complement. These direct tests will help determine whether the signature_c and signature_a findings are robust stratum effects or further evidence of arbitrary constructed-assay context modification. All accepted effects remain within-dataset associations, not causal claims or generalizable biological findings.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Iteration 17/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and voluntary validation is exhausted, so the next useful step is to sharpen the unresolved constructed-signature context layer with direct stratum estimates rather than adding speculative new biological axes. The accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association is large in high research_signature_b (stronger MDM2 dependency, raw negative exposed-minus-comparator, direction -1), but research_signature_c also mimics a similar CDKN2A-MDM2 context interaction. Existing active analyses test high signature_b/high signature_c together and low signature_b/high signature_c, as well as direct signature_c strata. The crucial missing complementary cell is direct estimation of the CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency inside high signature_b but low signature_c. I registered that as a new mean-difference hypothesis. Because more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency, the anticipated raw comparison is negative: CDKN2A-loss cells should have more negative MDM2 dependency scores than CDKN2A-intact cells if signature_b context is robust and not driven by co-occurring signature_c. With direction -1, a positive signed estimate therefore supports the accepted stronger-dependency direction. A small or null estimate would suggest that the high-signature_b CDKN2A-MDM2 pattern may be partly a co-occurrence or constructed-assay-context artifact rather than a signature_b-specific modifier. The alternatives are: (1) robust signature_b context modification if high-b/low-c remains substantial and consistent with high-b/high-c; (2) co-occurrence-dependent context if high-b effect largely vanishes when signature_c is low; or (3) imprecise estimate if stratum sizes are inadequate. This remains a within-dataset association analysis and does not establish causality or generalizability.

Priority 1 is direct stratum estimation of the mimicking signature patterns: H238/H239 estimate the CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency inside high versus lower research_signature_c; H240/H241 estimate the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency inside high versus lower research_signature_a. Iteration 17/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: No independent validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction. For direction -1 direct mean differences, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative: the exposed group has more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 direct mean differences, a positive signed estimate means the raw difference is positive, indicating a weaker dependency direction relative to exposed/comparator semantics. The new signature-context results substantially clarify the constructed-assay layer, while strengthening the conclusion that these are within-dataset associations rather than causal biology. H238 tests the direct CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency inside research_signature_c >= 0.5 and gives +0.390 [0.304, 0.475], about 1.7 MDM2 standard deviations and far above the approximate absolute-mean clinical benchmark. I accept it and close the claim. H239 tests the same direct effect inside research_signature_c <= 0.5 and gives +0.002 [-0.021, 0.025]. The effect is essentially null and the interval excludes clinically meaningful positive stronger-dependency evidence under the registered direction, so I reject and close that direct lower-signature_c claim. Together, H238/H239 convert the earlier signature_c interaction into direct stratum evidence: the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association is strongly concentrated in high research_signature_c. The co-occurrence grid is especially informative. H242 estimates the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 direct effect inside high research_signature_b and high research_signature_c and gives a very large +0.765 [0.692, 0.838]; H243 estimates lower signature_b with high signature_c and gives +0.207 [0.107, 0.307]; H244 estimates high signature_b and high signature_a and gives +0.304 [0.176, 0.432]. I accept these as supported within-dataset context associations. However, H245 is the decisive specificity control for signature_b alone: it estimates the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 effect inside high research_signature_b but low research_signature_c and gives only +0.024 [-0.015, 0.064]. The point estimate is small, not statistically supported, and does not provide a scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency claim. I reject H245 as a supported b-only direct effect and close it. Therefore, earlier accepted signature_b-associated CDKN2A-MDM2 effects should be interpreted as largely driven by co-occurring research_signature_c rather than signature_b being a specific independent modifier. H219 remains accepted because the threshold interaction estimate +0.180 [0.078, 0.282] is supported, but it is not evidence of signature_b specificity once H245 is considered. For PTEN-loss/STAT3, H240 gives a huge positive direction -1 direct effect in high research_signature_a, +0.604 [0.513, 0.695], and H241 gives a smaller but still substantial positive effect in lower research_signature_a, +0.115 [0.065, 0.165]. I accept both: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in both signature_a strata, but the effect is much stronger when research_signature_a is high. This supports signature_a as a context modifier of PTEN-STAT3, but not an all-or-nothing specificity claim. The TP53-context controls are mixed but mostly reassuring. H224 shows a large supported CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 direct effect in TP53-loss cells with high signature_b, +0.253 [0.076, 0.430], so that particular context effect is not explained away by TP53 status, though the 27-exposed-cell estimate is imprecise. H226 tests a registered positive direct PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect in high-signature_b TP53-intact cells; +0.026 [-0.024, 0.075] does not support a positive raw exposed-comparator difference, so I reject the specific claim, while noting that the accepted higher-level interaction evidence still supports attenuation relative to lower-signature_b cells. H227 is unresolved and closed because the cell is underpowered. Overall, I accept these new direct stratum results as within-dataset context associations, but I do not treat them as biologically assigned mechanisms or generalizable findings. The most important revision is that research_signature_b-specific context modification for CDKN2A/MDM2 is not supported when signature_c is low; research_signature_c and high-b/high-c co-occurrence provide the stronger direct effects.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation budget is exhausted, so exploration should now sharpen the remaining unresolved context layer without adding speculative biological claims. The key new evidence from the latest direct strata is that the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association is strongly concentrated in high research_signature_c, whereas the previously accepted research_signature_b-associated effect is largely explained when high research_signature_c is excluded. The next useful question is whether the high-signature_c CDKN2A-MDM2 association is robust to biologically and technically important conditions rather than being an artifact of one subgroup. I therefore registered direct strata of the CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency inside high research_signature_c split by TP53 status, screen ROC quality, KY-library status, and an extreme signature_c threshold. These are within-dataset association checks; if estimates remain substantial and intervals remain clear of zero and the clinical benchmark, the signature_c context effect can be interpreted as internally robust but still not causal or generalizable. I also registered specificity interactions for the other accepted headline exposures inside high research_signature_c: TP53 loss for USP7, SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2, PTEN loss for STAT3, and KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2. These are not meant to create new biological hypotheses but to test whether research_signature_c is an MDM2-associated assay-context modifier or a broadly general modifier of all dependency associations. For direction -1 direct mean differences, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 NFE2L2/KEAP1, positive signed estimates indicate the accepted weaker-dependency direction. For interactions with anticipated direction 0, supported nonzero estimates would indicate signature-context modification; null intervals would support specificity or lack of general modification. I also registered MTAP loss as a simple overall predictor of MDM2 dependency because prior analyses show CDKN2A is the stronger local axis, but MTAP co-occurrence could still make a simple biomarker useful. If MTAP is null or small relative to CDKN2A, that supports retaining CDKN2A rather than MTAP as the measured predictor. Finally, I registered a batch-A direct CDKN2A-MDM2 estimate and a high research_signature_a threshold PTEN-STAT3 direct estimate as technical/contextual refinement checks rather than new biological claims.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
No independent validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. All estimates below are already signed to the registered claim direction. For direction -1 direct MDM2 claims, a positive signed estimate means CDKN2A-loss cells have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 NFE2L2 claims, a positive signed estimate means the accepted weaker-dependency direction for KEAP1 loss. For interactions, a positive signed estimate means the effect is amplified in the named subgroup relative to its complement under the registered direction.

The new direct strata strongly support the high-research_signature_c concentration of the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association. H246 gives +0.385 [0.290, 0.480] in TP53-intact, high-signature-c cells; H247 gives +0.411 [0.198, 0.624] in TP53-loss, high-signature-c cells. The latter has a small exposed cell count, but the interval still clearly excludes zero, so the effect is robust enough to accept while noting imprecision. H248 gives +0.428 [0.312, 0.543] in high screen-ROC cells, H249 gives +0.415 [0.315, 0.515] in non-KY library cells, and H250 gives +0.406 [0.289, 0.523] in extreme signature-c cells. H256 gives +0.119 [0.052, 0.187] in batch A, consistent with the already validated overall CDKN2A-MDM2 effect. I therefore accept and close H246-H250 and H256. These are within-dataset robustness checks for the association, not evidence of causality or external generalizability.

The specificity controls mostly support selectivity of the high-signature-c modification for MDM2. H251, the interaction of TP53 loss and high signature_c for USP7 dependency, gives a small positive signed estimate +0.031 [-0.013, 0.075]; the interval includes zero, so the registered amplification claim is not supported. H252 for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 gives +0.007 [-0.034, 0.048], essentially null. H254 for KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 gives -0.010 [-0.050, 0.031], also null under the registered direction. H255 for MTAP loss as an overall predictor of MDM2 dependency gives only +0.019 [-0.008, 0.045]; this is small, statistically unresolved, and below the rough 10% absolute-mean benchmark for MDM2, so MTAP alone is not supported as a useful simple predictor. I reject and close H251, H252, H254, and H255.

H253 is more informative than a simple null. For the PTEN-loss/STAT3 interaction with high research_signature_c, the signed estimate under the registered direction -1 is -0.163 [-0.270, -0.056]. Because this is negative when signed to direction -1, the raw interaction is opposite to the registered hypothesis: PTEN loss appears associated with less strong STAT3 dependency in high-signature-c cells relative to the complement. This magnitude is large relative to STAT3 dependency scale and exceeds the 10% benchmark, but it does not support H253 as registered. I therefore reject H253 in its original direction. I keep H253 active and register refinements: a reversed-direction interaction claim and direct PTEN-loss/STAT3 estimates in high versus low signature_c. These are exploratory refinements motivated by R221 and are needed to determine whether the attenuation is robust and whether the PTEN effect remains present but weaker in high signature_c.

H257 tests a high research_signature_a threshold for PTEN loss/STAT3 dependency and gives a very large +0.627 [0.500, 0.755] signed estimate under direction -1. This strongly supports the already observed signature_a context modification of PTEN-STAT3, while again remaining an internal association rather than a causal mechanism.

Multiplicity and causal interpretation are important. The CDKN2A-MDM2 signature-c strata are large, internally consistent across TP53 status, screen quality, library type, extreme signature-c, and batch A, which makes false-positive interpretation less plausible, but they still reflect constructed assay context rather than biological assignment. The null interactions for USP7, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2 support MDM2-selective context modification, while H253 suggests that signature_c may also attenuate at least one unrelated PTEN-STAT3 association. Therefore the strongest supported conclusion is that high research_signature_c sharply concentrates the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association, but it is not a uniform modifier of all accepted dependency associations.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

expectation

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
No new validation was released, assessments_due is empty, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so synthesis is based on the accumulated discovery and prior validation evidence. The headline dataset-supported dependency associations are large, internally coherent, and mostly independently validated. TP53 non-loss versus TP53 loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, with validated signed effect +0.811 [0.782, 0.841]; equivalently TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency. SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, validated +0.805 [0.774, 0.836]. MSI-high versus MSS is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, validated +0.790 [0.736, 0.843]. KEAP1 loss versus non-loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; after direction correction the validated estimate is +0.802 [0.775, 0.829]. PTEN loss versus non-loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, validated overall +0.292 [0.213, 0.370] and strong in the TP53-loss stratum +0.442 [0.265, 0.619]. CDKN2A loss versus non-loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, validated overall +0.114 [0.067, 0.161], TP53-intact +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and low copy_number_9p21 +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. These effects are large on the dependency-score scale and well above the practical 10 percent clinical-significance benchmark. Some highly conditioned CDKN2A-MDM2 strata are smaller and less certain, for example the TP53-intact/MTAP-intact/low-9p21 validated effect +0.085 [0.004, 0.166] has a lower bound near zero, so it should not be promoted as a uniformly large conditional effect.

The context-assay findings are internal associations rather than biological mechanisms. High research_signature_c sharply concentrates the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association: accepted direct estimates are +0.385 [0.290, 0.480] in TP53-intact, +0.411 [0.198, 0.624] in TP53-loss, +0.428 [0.312, 0.543] in high screen-quality cells, +0.415 [0.315, 0.515] in non-KY library cells, +0.406 [0.289, 0.523] in extreme signature-c cells, and +0.119 [0.052, 0.187] in batch A. This pattern is internally robust, but it reflects a constructed assay context and does not establish causality or external generalizability. High research_signature_a also amplifies PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency, with an extreme high-signature-a estimate +0.627 [0.500, 0.755]. I now reassess the signature-c PTEN-STAT3 interaction. H253 remains rejected as originally registered because the signed discovery estimate is -0.163 [-0.270, -0.056], meaning the raw interaction is opposite to the anticipated amplification. The reversed claim H258 is accepted because the same evidence signed to the reverse direction is +0.163 [0.056, 0.270], indicating that PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is meaningfully attenuated in high research_signature_c relative to its complement. This is an important within-dataset context finding, but direct high-versus-low signature_c PTEN-STAT3 strata are still needed to quantify whether the attenuated high-signature-c association remains substantial.

Important negative or null findings bound the conclusions. KRAS mutation does not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not predict EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict ERBB2 dependency. TP53 loss is not a simple MDM2-dependency driver in the reciprocal direction; MTAP loss is weak or null after conditioning on CDKN2A, and simple MTAP-alone MDM2 dependency is not supported. CDKN2A loss does not spill over onto USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 and does not predict MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, or TMED10 dependency in the broad tests. Constructed markers D/E/F and many technical strata mostly provide negative controls or unresolved low-count contexts; they do not add general biological roles. Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly in low-count technical or lineage strata, batch-A PTEN-STAT3 validation, the small lower bound of one conditioned CDKN2A-MDM2 stratum, and direct high-versus-low research_signature_c PTEN-STAT3 estimates. If further analysis is allowed, the most informative next step is to analyze H259 and H260, the direct PTEN-loss/STAT3 mean differences inside high and low research_signature_c strata, because they will show whether attenuation by signature-c is a residual but reduced PTEN effect or a near-null effect. Secondary controls such as marker-F and APC negative tests can be retained only if capacity remains.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

For interactions, a positive signed estimate means the effect is amplified in the named subgroup relative to its complement under the registered direction.\n\nThe new direct strata strongly support the high-research_signature_c concentration of the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association. H246 gives +0.385 [0.290, 0.480] in TP53-intact, high-signature-c cells; H247 gives +0.411 [0.198, 0.624] in TP53-loss, high-signature-c cells. These are within-dataset robustness checks for the association, not evidence of causality or external generalizability.\n\nThe specificity controls mostly support selectivity of the high-signature-c modification for MDM2.
