H252 for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 gives +0.007 [-0.034, 0.048], essentially null. H254 for KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 gives -0.010 [-0.050, 0.031], also null under the registered direction. H255 for MTAP loss as an overall predictor of MDM2 dependency gives only +0.019 [-0.008, 0.045]; this is small, statistically unresolved, and below the rough 10% absolute-mean benchmark for MDM2, so MTAP alone is not supported as a useful simple predictor. I reject and close H251, H252, H254, and H255.\n\nH253 is more informative than a simple null. For the PTEN-loss/STAT3 interaction with high research_signature_c, the signed estimate under the registered direction -1 is -0.163 [-0.270, -0.056]. Because this is negative when signed to direction -1, the raw interaction is opposite to the registered hypothesis: PTEN loss appears associated with less strong STAT3 dependency in high-signature-c cells relative to the complement. This magnitude is large relative to STAT3 dependency scale and exceeds the 10% benchmark, but it does not support H253 as registered. I therefore reject H253 in its original direction. I keep H253 active and register refinements: a reversed-direction interaction claim and direct PTEN-loss/STAT3 estimates in high versus low signature_c. These are exploratory refinements motivated by R221 and are needed to determine whether the attenuation is robust and whether the PTEN effect remains present but weaker in high signature_c.\n\nH257 tests a high research_signature_a threshold for PTEN loss/STAT3 dependency and gives a very large +0.627 [0.500, 0.755] signed estimate under direction -1. This strongly supports the already observed signature_a context modification of PTEN-STAT3, while again remaining an internal association rather than a causal mechanism.\n\nMultiplicity and causal interpretation are important. The CDKN2A-MDM2 signature-c strata are large, internally consistent across TP53 status, screen quality, library type, extreme signature-c, and batch A, which makes false-positive interpretation less plausible, but they still reflect constructed assay context rather than biological assignment. The null interactions for USP7, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2 support MDM2-selective context modification, while H253 suggests that signature_c may also attenuate at least one unrelated PTEN-STAT3 association. Therefore the strongest supported conclusion is that high research_signature_c sharply concentrates the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association, but it is not a uniform modifier of all accepted dependency associations.","synthesize":"No new validation was released, assessments_due is empty, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so synthesis is based on the accumulated discovery and prior validation evidence. The headline dataset-supported dependency associations are large, internally coherent, and mostly independently validated. TP53 non-loss versus TP53 loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, with validated signed effect +0.811 [0.782, 0.841]; equivalently TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency. SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, validated +0.805 [0.774, 0.836]. MSI-high versus MSS is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, validated +0.790 [0.736, 0.843]. KEAP1 loss versus non-loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; after direction correction the validated estimate is +0.802 [0.775, 0.829]. PTEN loss versus non-loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, validated overall +0.292 [0.213, 0.370] and strong in the TP53-loss stratum +0.442 [0.265, 0.619]. CDKN2A loss versus non-loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, validated overall +0.114 [0.067, 0.161], TP53-intact +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and low copy_number_9p21 +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. These effects are large on the dependency-score scale and well above the practical 10 percent clinical-significance benchmark. Some highly conditioned CDKN2A-MDM2 strata are smaller and less certain, for example the TP53-intact/MTAP-intact/low-9p21 validated effect +0.085 [0.004, 0.166] has a lower bound near zero, so it should not be promoted as a uniformly large conditional effect.\n\nThe context-assay findings are internal associations rather than biological mechanisms. High research_signature_c sharply concentrates the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association: accepted direct estimates are +0.385 [0.290, 0.480] in TP53-intact, +0.411 [0.198, 0.624] in TP53-loss, +0.428 [0.312, 0.543] in high screen-quality cells, +0.415 [0.315, 0.515] in non-KY library cells, +0.406 [0.289, 0.523] in extreme signature-c cells, and +0.119 [0.052, 0.187] in batch A. This pattern is internally robust, but it reflects a constructed assay context and does not establish causality or external generalizability. High research_signature_a also amplifies PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency, with an extreme high-signature-a estimate +0.627 [0.500, 0.755]. I now reassess the signature-c PTEN-STAT3 interaction. H253 remains rejected as originally registered because the signed discovery estimate is -0.163 [-0.270, -0.056], meaning the raw interaction is opposite to the anticipated amplification. The reversed claim H258 is accepted because the same evidence signed to the reverse direction is +0.163 [0.056, 0.270], indicating that PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is meaningfully attenuated in high research_signature_c relative to its complement. This is an important within-dataset context finding, but direct high-versus-low signature_c PTEN-STAT3 strata are still needed to quantify whether the attenuated high-signature-c association remains substantial.\n\nImportant negative or null findings bound the conclusions. KRAS mutation does not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not predict EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict ERBB2 dependency. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation budget is exhausted, so this analyze stage focuses on untested discovery analyses that resolve the remaining registered context structure and complete direct strata for a few accepted headline axes. I request eight active constructed-signature context claims plus four deferred direct robustness claims. H259 and H260 provide absolute PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency effects in high and low research_signature_c, respectively, which are needed to interpret the reversed interaction H258: attenuation may mean a smaller residual effect or an approximately abolished effect. H261 through H264 decompose the research_signature_c by research_signature_a 2x2 for PTEN-loss/STAT3 and test whether high signature_a modifies or overcomes high signature_c attenuation. H265 and H266 test whether the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 context effect persists when one constructed signature is high and the other is low, helping distinguish signature_c-specific context modification from broad signature-context modification. H37 and H38 give direct KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2-dependency estimates in TP53-loss and TP53-intact strata, completing biological robustness checks after the TP53-interaction test. For PTEN/STAT3, USP7/SMARCA2, and MDM2 claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate indicates the registered stronger-dependency direction. For NFE2L2 claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate indicates the accepted weaker-dependency direction. record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For the direction -1 STAT3 and MDM2 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed genetic or loss state is associated with a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For the direction +1 NFE2L2 claims, a positive signed estimate means the accepted weaker NFE2L2 dependency direction for KEAP1 loss. Validation requests are unavailable because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so these are discovery-evidence assessments only and do not establish external generalizability.  The new direct research_signature_c strata clarify the PTEN-loss STAT3 context effect. H259 gives +0.156 with 95% interval [0.071, 0.242] in high research_signature_c cells, while H260 gives +0.319 with [0.255, 0.384] in low research_signature_c cells. This supports the previously accepted reversed interaction interpretation: PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in high signature_c cells, but the effect is substantially attenuated relative to low signature_c. The point estimate is above the 10% practical benchmark, although the lower confidence bound is below 10%, so the residual high-signature-c effect is statistically robust and moderate but less certain as a clinically significant effect. I therefore accept H259 and H260 and close them.  The four research_signature_c by research_signature_a cells make the PTEN STAT3 context structure more specific. prompt:
Iteration 20/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

This association is robust across TP53 strata, lineage, STK11 strata, library, culture, batch A, and screen-quality strata, and no TP53 interaction was supported. This is a moderate but reproducible main effect and is amplified in TP53-loss cells, validated +0.442 [0.265, 0.619], discovery +0.190 [0.085, 0.296]. It remains positive in many technical and mutation strata, including screen-quality strata, KRAS-mutated and KRAS-nonmutated cells, PIK3CA strata, adherent culture, adenocarcinoma, and non-KY-library cells. Sixth, CDKN2A loss versus non-loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, validated overall +0.114 [0.067, 0.161], discovery +0.117 [0.082, 0.152]. This is a smaller but internally robust association, strongest in TP53-intact cells, validated +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and in low copy_number_9p21 cells, validated +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. The constructed-signature analyses identify within-dataset context modification rather than assigned biological mechanisms. For PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, high research_signature_a amplifies the association: direct high-signature-a +0.604 [0.513, 0.695] and extreme high-signature-a +0.627 [0.500, 0.755]. Conversely, high research_signature_c attenuates the PTEN-loss STAT3 effect relative to its complement, accepted reversed interaction +0.163 [0.056, 0.270], while the original amplification interaction was rejected. Direct strata quantify this: high signature_c +0.156 [0.071, 0.242] and low signature_c +0.319 [0.255, 0.384]. The 2x2 signature_c by signature_a decomposition supports the same interpretation: high signature_a with low signature_c +0.648 [0.548, 0.749]; high signature_c with high signature_a +0.469 [0.253, 0.685] but with only 20 exposed cells, so precision is limited; low signature_c with low signature_a +0.144 [0.080, 0.209]; and high signature_c with low signature_a +0.060 [-0.020, 0.140], rejected as too small and statistically unresolved. Thus, in this dataset, PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is primarily amplified by signature_a and attenuated by signature_c, with signature_a able to retain a large effect even in high-signature-c cells, while high signature_c without high signature_a leaves little residual PTEN effect. For CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency, high research_signature_c sharply concentrates the association: direct high signature_c +0.390 [0.304, 0.475], high signature_c low signature_a +0.334 [0.230, 0.437], high signature_b high signature_c +0.765 [0.692, 0.838], and direct high signature_c +0.207 [0.107, 0.307] when signature_b is low. By contrast, high signature_a with low signature_c is essentially null and rejected, signed -0.010 [-0.057, 0.038]. The CDKN2A-MDM2 context effect is also internally accepted in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, high screen-quality, non-KY-library, and batch-A strata. This pattern supports signature_c-specific context concentration for MDM2 rather than a broad signature-context effect driven by signature_a. The last missing cell in this 2x2 is low signature_c with low signature_a, registered but not yet tested.\n\nNegative and bounded findings. Several biologically obvious matched driver associations were negative: KRAS mutation does not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not predict EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict ERBB2 dependency. EGFR amplification also did not predict KRAS or TMED10 dependency in the broad tests. TP53 loss is not a simple MDM2-dependency driver in the tested direction; the MDM2 effect is instead centered on CDKN2A loss. MTAP loss is weak or null after conditioning on CDKN2A, and simple MTAP-alone MDM2 dependency is not supported. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 and was negative for MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, and BRAF dependency. CDKN2A loss does not spill over onto USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 dependency. Constructed markers D, E, and F mostly act as negative controls or low-information strata. Many technical or batch interactions remain unresolved or closed as not scientifically central; they do not overturn the core accepted associations.\n\nCausality and generalizability. All conclusions are dataset-supported associations among measured predictors, constructed assays, and CRISPR dependency scores. The research signatures and markers have no assigned gene or pathway, so context effects should be described as assay-context modification, not mechanism. The dataset is a single lung-cell-line CRISPR screen setting with lineage subtype and technical assay heterogeneity; even independent validation intervals account for within-study validation comparisons, not external cohort replication. Causality, therapeutic relevance, and generalization to external populations remain unestablished.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty and next analysis. The main remaining uncertainty is the untested low research_signature_c by low research_signature_a CDKN2A-loss MDM2 cell, H267. Analyzing H267 is the single most informative next step because it completes the 2x2 context decomposition. If H267 is near null or small, the MDM2 context effect is signature_c-specific. If H267 is substantial, the effect should be reframed as broad assay-context modification rather than signature_c specificity. Batch-A PTEN-STAT3 also remains unresolved because validation crossed zero. These caveats should limit, but not reverse, the accepted pattern: PTEN-STAT3 is robust overall but context-modified, and CDKN2A-MDM2 is robust overall but context concentrated."}}

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this exploration adds discovery comparisons that complete the remaining context structure and test specificity/robustness of the strongest accepted associations. For direction -1 dependency-score claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed predictor is associated with a more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency score. For the NFE2L2 direction +1 claim, a positive signed estimate means the accepted weaker NFE2L2 dependency direction after KEAP1 loss. First, I register the missing high research_signature_c/high research_signature_a CDKN2A-loss MDM2 direct stratum. Together with active H267 low-C/low-A, accepted H266 high-C/low-A, and rejected H265 high-A/low-C, this completes the 2x2 context decomposition and clarifies whether the MDM2 context effect is primarily signature-c driven, with high signature_a allowed to coexist, or whether broad high-signature context modification is needed. Second, I register a sensitivity analysis for the PTEN-loss STAT3 high-A/high-C association using a lower signature-c threshold to increase exposed cells and assess whether the small-n H262 high-high cell reflects a reproducible large effect. Third, I register direct high-signature-a strata for USP7/TP53 non-loss, SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, WRN/MSI-high, and NFE2L2/KEAP1 loss. These are not designed to discover new strong main associations but to test whether signature_a modification is specific to the PTEN-STAT3 axis rather than a generic amplifier across the accepted dependency axes. If these core axes remain large and comparable to their overall effects in high-signature-a cells, this supports signature_a as a context-specific amplifier; if they are attenuated, the signature context interpretation should be broadened. Finally, I register a CDKN2A-loss MDM2 interaction by batch_a and two direct robustness strata for the high-signature-c CDKN2A-MDM2 effect in lower-screen-quality and KY-library cells. These address whether the large accepted context effect is artifact-prone, although they remain within-dataset associations and do not establish causal biology or external generalizability.

Iteration 20/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed state is associated with a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score; for the direction +1 NFE2L2 claim, a positive signed estimate is consistent with the accepted weaker NFE2L2 dependency direction after KEAP1 loss. No new independent validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so these are discovery-evidence assessments and do not establish causality or external generalizability. I use a practical benchmark of roughly 0.10 dependency-score units, which is conservative relative to a 10% relative change for these centered negative scores, and I require the interval and point estimate to support a meaningful difference rather than merely a small statistical deviation. H267 is near null, +0.0066 [-0.0192, 0.0324], with the confidence interval including no effect and the upper bound well below the practical benchmark. If the delivered stratum is the intended low-context CDKN2A-MDM2 cell, this supports the emerging pattern that high research_signature_c is the main context driver rather than a broad high-signature context. However, the displayed H267 eligibility appears to overlap an earlier accepted low-9p21 stratum while the delivered cell counts differ, so I flag this as a registration or display ambiguity. I do not use this null result to overturn the validated CDKN2A-MDM2 main association, but I registered an explicit low-signature-c and low-signature-a stratum to remove the ambiguity. H268 gives a large CDKN2A-loss MDM2 effect in high signature_c and high signature_a, +0.490 [0.340, 0.641], supporting that high signature_c concentrates the association even when signature_a is also high. Together with the rejected high-signature-a/low-signature-c stratum, this favors signature-c-specific context modification rather than a generic signature_a amplifier for MDM2. H269 is a higher-n sensitivity analysis for PTEN-loss STAT3 in high signature_a using a lower signature_c threshold, +0.549 [0.386, 0.713] with only 29 exposed cells. The interval is entirely above the practical benchmark, so I accept it with caution about small-cell precision. This continues to support high signature_a as an amplifier of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. H270 through H273 are direct high-signature-a strata for the core USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 axes. All four are very large and intervals are far above the practical benchmark: USP7 +0.823 [0.788, 0.857], SMARCA2 +0.785 [0.750, 0.819], WRN +0.799 [0.739, 0.860], and NFE2L2 direction +1 +0.798 [0.758, 0.837]. These support that the core dependencies remain extremely strong in high signature_a, and they do not indicate that signature_a generally attenuates the core axes. The high-signature-a amplification is most distinctive for PTEN-loss STAT3. H272 has only 31 exposed MSI-high cells, but the interval is so far above the benchmark that acceptance is reasonable within this dataset. H274 tests whether the high-signature-c CDKN2A-MDM2 association is modified by batch_a, +0.003 [-0.076, 0.081]. This is small, statistically unresolved, and the upper bound is below the practical benchmark, so I reject it as a meaningful interaction. H275 and H276 show that the high-signature-c CDKN2A-MDM2 effect remains large in lower screen-quality cells and in KY-library cells, +0.336 [0.207, 0.466] and +0.305 [0.134, 0.475] respectively; I accept both, with caution in H276 because exposed n is 27. These support technical robustness of the signature_c context effect, although they remain within-dataset associations. H27, TP53 loss for KIF18A dependency, is signed positive, +0.021 [0.001, 0.040]. It may be statistically small-positive, but the point estimate is far below the practical benchmark and the interval does not robustly exceed even a relative 10% scale for this outcome. I reject it as scientifically or practically meaningful. H28, MYC amplification for RPL11 dependency, is opposite the registered direction and unresolved, -0.012 [-0.034, 0.009], so I reject it. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the core dependency associations, refines the constructed-signature context interpretation, and rejects small residual direct effects that are statistically detectable but not practically meaningful.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Six core dependency associations are supported by large discovery effects and, for the main versions, independent validation. First, TP53 status is strongly associated with USP7 dependency: TP53 non-loss versus TP53 loss has validated signed effect +0.811 [0.782, 0.841], with discovery +0.802 [0.782, 0.822]. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed state is associated with a more negative, stronger dependency score; for the accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2 direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency after KEAP1 loss.\n\nValidation and deadline assessment: none new. Existing validation for USP7/TP53, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI-high, NFE2L2/KEAP1, STAT3/PTEN overall and TP53-loss subgroup, MDM2/CDKN2A overall and TP53-intact and low-9p21 strata, and SMARCA4 interaction by ARID1A remains informative. All independent intervals are within-study validation intervals and account for the maximum number of validation comparisons, not external replication.\n\nSupported core findings. 1) TP53 non-loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss: discovery +0.802 [0.782, 0.822], independent validation +0.811 [0.782, 0.841]. This is among the largest accepted effects and remains large in many internal strata, including adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, high and lower screen quality, KY and non-KY library, batch A, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, aneuploidy strata, and high research_signature_a +0.823 [0.788, 0.857]. 2) SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803], validation +0.805 [0.774, 0.836]. This synthetic-lethality-like association is robust across ARID1A strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch, STK11-loss cells, KY and non-KY library, and high research_signature_a +0.785 [0.750, 0.819]. 3) MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: discovery +0.790 [0.760, 0.819], validation +0.790 [0.736, 0.843]. It is robust across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, and high research_signature_a +0.799 [0.739, 0.860], though some strata have small exposed counts. 4) KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, after correcting the registered direction: discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816], validation +0.802 [0.775, 0.829]. It is robust across TP53, lineage, STK11, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, and high research_signature_a +0.798 [0.758, 0.837]. 5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery +0.267 [0.215, 0.319], validation +0.292 [0.213, 0.370]. The effect is moderate but reproducible and is amplified in TP53-loss cells: discovery +0.190 [0.085, 0.296], validation +0.442 [0.265, 0.619]. It remains positive in many technical and mutation strata, although batch-A validation crossed zero and remains unresolved. 6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: discovery +0.117 [0.082, 0.152], validation +0.114 [0.067, 0.161]. This is a smaller but internally robust association, strongest in TP53-intact cells, validated +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and in low copy_number_9p21 cells, validated +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the core dependency associations, refines the constructed-signature context interpretation, and rejects small residual direct effects that are statistically detectable but not practically meaningful.","synthesize":"No new validation was released in this iteration, and no response deadlines are pending. The voluntary validation budget is exhausted; therefore no new independent validation can be requested. No claims were due for assessment, so I made no status changes. The following synthesis incorporates the existing validations already recorded in the ledger. I use a conservative practical benchmark of about 0.10 absolute signed dependency-score units, because a 10% relative change is difficult to interpret for centered negative CRISPR scores. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed state is associated with a more negative, stronger dependency score; for the accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2 direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency after KEAP1 loss.\n\nValidation and deadline assessment: none new. Existing validation for USP7/TP53, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI-high, NFE2L2/KEAP1, STAT3/PTEN overall and TP53-loss subgroup, MDM2/CDKN2A overall and TP53-intact and low-9p21 strata, and SMARCA4 interaction by ARID1A remains informative. All independent intervals are within-study validation intervals and account for the maximum number of validation comparisons, not external replication.\n\nSupported core findings. 1) TP53 non-loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss: discovery +0.802 [0.782, 0.822], independent validation +0.811 [0.782, 0.841]. This is among the largest accepted effects and remains large in many internal strata, including adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, high and lower screen quality, KY and non-KY library, batch A, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, aneuploidy strata, and high research_signature_a +0.823 [0.788, 0.857]. 2) SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803], validation +0.805 [0.774, 0.836]. This synthetic-lethality-like association is robust across ARID1A strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch, STK11-loss cells, KY and non-KY library, and high research_signature_a +0.785 [0.750, 0.819]. 3) MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: discovery +0.790 [0.760, 0.819], validation +0.790 [0.736, 0.843]. It is robust across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, and high research_signature_a +0.799 [0.739, 0.860], though some strata have small exposed counts. 4) KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, after correcting the registered direction: discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816], validation +0.802 [0.775, 0.829]. It is robust across TP53, lineage, STK11, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, and high research_signature_a +0.798 [0.758, 0.837]. 5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery +0.267 [0.215, 0.319], validation +0.292 [0.213, 0.370]. The effect is moderate but reproducible and is amplified in TP53-loss cells: discovery +0.190 [0.085, 0.296], validation +0.442 [0.265, 0.619]. It remains positive in many technical and mutation strata, although batch-A validation crossed zero and remains unresolved. 6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: discovery +0.117 [0.082, 0.152], validation +0.114 [0.067, 0.161]. This is a smaller but internally robust association, strongest in TP53-intact cells, validated +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and in low copy_number_9p21 cells, validated +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. TP53 loss by itself is not supported as a simple MDM2 driver in the originally tested direction.\n\nContext-specific findings. The constructed research signatures modify two moderate axes but should not be interpreted as assigned biological pathways. For PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, high research_signature_a amplifies the association: high signature_a direct +0.604 [0.513, 0.695], extreme high signature_a +0.627 [0.500, 0.755], and the signature_a interaction +0.489 [0.385, 0.593]. High research_signature_c attenuates the PTEN effect: the reversed signature_c interaction is accepted at +0.163 [0.056, 0.270], with direct high signature_c +0.156 [0.071, 0.242] and low signature_c +0.319 [0.255, 0.384]. The completed signature_c by signature_a decomposition shows: high A low C +0.648 [0.548, 0.749]; high C high A +0.469 [0.253, 0.685] but only 20 exposed cells; low C low A +0.144 [0.080, 0.209]; high C low A +0.060 [-0.020, 0.140], rejected. High signature_b also attenuates: high signature_b direct +0.018 [-0.025, 0.061] rejected and low signature_b +0.392 [0.327, 0.457] accepted, with a reversed high-signature-b interaction +0.411 [0.333, 0.488]. Together, PTEN-STAT3 is most strongly expressed in high signature_a and low signature_b/signature_c contexts. For CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency, high research_signature_c concentrates the association: direct high signature_c +0.390 [0.304, 0.475], high C low A +0.334 [0.230, 0.437], high B high C +0.765 [0.692, 0.838], and high C low B +0.207 [0.107, 0.307]. By contrast, high signature_a with low signature_c is null and rejected, -0.010 [-0.057, 0.038]. The completed low signature_c by low signature_a cell, delivered as H277, is near null and rejected, +0.0066 [-0.019, 0.0324], resolving the prior duplicate-registration ambiguity around H267. The MDM2 context effect remains large in lower screen-quality cells +0.336 [0.207, 0.466] and KY-library cells +0.305 [0.134, 0.475], and it is not modified by batch A, interaction +0.003 [-0.076, 0.081]. Thus, the MDM2 context pattern is signature-c-specific, with signature_b able to amplify further, rather than a generic high-signature effect.\n\nNegative and bounded findings. Driver-matched associations that might be biologically expected are negative in this dataset: KRAS mutation does not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not predict EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict ERBB2 dependency. EGFR amplification also did not predict KRAS or TMED10 dependency in broad tests. TP53 loss is not a simple MDM2 driver in the tested direction; MTAP loss is weak or null after conditioning on CDKN2A, and MTAP-alone MDM2 dependency is not supported. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 and was rejected for MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, and BRAF dependency. CDKN2A loss does not spill over onto USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 dependency. Several direct predictor tests were small but statistically detectable, such as TP53 loss for KIF18A +0.021 [0.001, 0.040], and were rejected as not practically meaningful. Research markers D, E, and F mostly behave as low-information or negative-control strata. Many technical or batch interactions remain unresolved or were closed as not scientifically central; these do not overturn the core accepted associations.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. The voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so remaining unresolved items rely on discovery intervals or previously returned validation. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The following synthesis incorporates the existing validations already recorded in the ledger. I use a conservative practical benchmark of about 0.10 absolute signed dependency-score units, because a 10% relative change is difficult to interpret for centered negative CRISPR scores. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed state is associated with a more negative, stronger dependency score; for the accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2 direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency after KEAP1 loss.\n\nValidation and deadline assessment: none new. Existing validation for USP7/TP53, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI-high, NFE2L2/KEAP1, STAT3/PTEN overall and TP53-loss subgroup, MDM2/CDKN2A overall and TP53-intact and low-9p21 strata, and SMARCA4 interaction by ARID1A remains informative. All independent intervals are within-study validation intervals and account for the maximum number of validation comparisons, not external replication.\n\nSupported core findings. 1) TP53 non-loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss: discovery +0.802 [0.782, 0.822], independent validation +0.811 [0.782, 0.841]. This is among the largest accepted effects and remains large in many internal strata, including adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, high and lower screen quality, KY and non-KY library, batch A, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, aneuploidy strata, and high research_signature_a +0.823 [0.788, 0.857]. 2) SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803], validation +0.805 [0.774, 0.836]. This synthetic-lethality-like association is robust across ARID1A strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch, STK11-loss cells, KY and non-KY library, and high research_signature_a +0.785 [0.750, 0.819]. 3) MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: discovery +0.790 [0.760, 0.819], validation +0.790 [0.736, 0.843]. It is robust across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, and high research_signature_a +0.799 [0.739, 0.860], though some strata have small exposed counts. 4) KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, after correcting the registered direction: discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816], validation +0.802 [0.775, 0.829]. It is robust across TP53, lineage, STK11, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, and high research_signature_a +0.798 [0.758, 0.837]. 5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery +0.267 [0.215, 0.319], validation +0.292 [0.213, 0.370]. The effect is moderate but reproducible and is amplified in TP53-loss cells: discovery +0.190 [0.085, 0.296], validation +0.442 [0.265, 0.619]. It remains positive in many technical and mutation strata, although batch-A validation crossed zero and remains unresolved. 6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: discovery +0.117 [0.082, 0.152], validation +0.114 [0.067, 0.161]. This is a smaller but internally robust association, strongest in TP53-intact cells, validated +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and in low copy_number_9p21 cells, validated +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. TP53 loss by itself is not supported as a simple MDM2 driver in the originally tested direction.\n\nContext-specific findings. The constructed research signatures modify two moderate axes but should not be interpreted as assigned biological pathways. For PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, high research_signature_a amplifies the association: high signature_a direct +0.604 [0.513, 0.695], extreme high signature_a +0.627 [0.500, 0.755], and the signature_a interaction +0.489 [0.385, 0.593]. High research_signature_c attenuates the PTEN effect: the reversed signature_c interaction is accepted at +0.163 [0.056, 0.270], with direct high signature_c +0.156 [0.071, 0.242] and low signature_c +0.319 [0.255, 0.384]. The completed signature_c by signature_a decomposition shows: high A low C +0.648 [0.548, 0.749]; high C high A +0.469 [0.253, 0.685] but only 20 exposed cells; low C low A +0.144 [0.080, 0.209]; high C low A +0.060 [-0.020, 0.140], rejected. High signature_b also attenuates: high signature_b direct +0.018 [-0.025, 0.061] rejected and low signature_b +0.392 [0.327, 0.457] accepted, with a reversed high-signature-b interaction +0.411 [0.333, 0.488]. Together, PTEN-STAT3 is most strongly expressed in high signature_a and low signature_b/signature_c contexts. For CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency, high research_signature_c concentrates the association: direct high signature_c +0.390 [0.304, 0.475], high C low A +0.334 [0.230, 0.437], high B high C +0.765 [0.692, 0.838], and high C low B +0.207 [0.107, 0.307]. By contrast, high signature_a with low signature_c is null and rejected, -0.010 [-0.057, 0.038]. The completed low signature_c by low signature_a cell, delivered as H277, is near null and rejected, +0.0066 [-0.019, 0.0324], resolving the prior duplicate-registration ambiguity around H267. The MDM2 context effect remains large in lower screen-quality cells +0.336 [0.207, 0.466] and KY-library cells +0.305 [0.134, 0.475], and it is not modified by batch A, interaction +0.003 [-0.076, 0.081]. Thus, the MDM2 context pattern is signature-c-specific, with signature_b able to amplify further, rather than a generic high-signature effect.\n\nNegative and bounded findings. Driver-matched associations that might be biologically expected are negative in this dataset: KRAS mutation does not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not predict EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict ERBB2 dependency. record.narrative: No independent validation budget remains, so all judgments below are discovery-evidence assessments and are not claims of causality or external generalizability. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean the exposed state is associated with a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score; for H281, direction +1 positive estimates correspond to the accepted weaker NFE2L2 dependency after KEAP1 loss. H278 through H281 complete the low research_signature_a decomposition of the core axes: USP7 non-loss TP53 +0.792 [0.768,0.816], SMARCA2 loss SMARCA4 +0.783 [0.760,0.807], WRN MSI-high +0.787 [0.753,0.822], and NFE2L2 KEAP1 loss +0.796 [0.772,0.820]. All are far above the practical benchmark and intervals are very tight; accept and close. These results indicate that low constructed signature_a does not attenuate the core dependencies. H284 through H287 test robustness in high biological-state strata: USP7 in high EMT +0.785 [0.750,0.820], SMARCA2 in high stemness +0.792 [0.754,0.830], WRN in high hypoxia +0.778 [0.720,0.835], and NFE2L2 in high IFN-gamma signature +0.792 [0.752,0.831]. All are very large and accept closed, though H286 has only 31 exposed MSI-high cells and should be read as imprecise but strongly supportive within dataset. H282 gives the direct high research_signature_a CDKN2A-loss MDM2 mean difference +0.163 [0.091,0.236]. I accept this as a meaningful subgroup association because the point estimate and upper interval exceed the practical benchmark, but I do not treat it as evidence that signature_a specifically modifies CDKN2A-MDM2 biology: the corresponding high-signature_a interaction was rejected and high signature_a contains subgroups defined by signature_b and signature_c. H283 gives direct low signature_a +0.096 [0.057,0.134]. The point estimate is below the practical benchmark and the interval is not robustly above it; reject this specific low-signature_a difference as independently meaningful, while retaining the overall accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association. H289 and H290 test MYC RNA strata for CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency: high MYC RNA +0.111 [0.060,0.163] and low MYC RNA +0.104 [0.047,0.161]. Both are around the overall effect, intervals exclude the null, and point estimates exceed the benchmark; accept them with caution about lower-bound precision. Because the high- and low-MYC estimates are similar, these direct strata support a broadly retained CDKN2A-MDM2 association rather than a clear MYC-expression context modification. The multiplicity of constructed-signature and biological-state tests requires conservative interpretation. Remaining residual specificity/context claims H288, H291, H292, and H293 are deferred as low priority: PTEN-loss STAT3 in high hypoxia is unlikely to add beyond accepted signature context, PTEN specificity beyond STAT3 is largely complete, and TP53-loss POLR2A is exploratory unless analyze prioritizes it.

The voluntary validation budget is exhausted; therefore no new independent validation can be requested. No claims were due for assessment, so I made no status changes. The following synthesis incorporates the existing validations already recorded in the ledger. I use a conservative practical benchmark of about 0.10 absolute signed dependency-score units, because a 10% relative change is difficult to interpret for centered negative CRISPR scores. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed state is associated with a more negative, stronger dependency score; for the accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2 direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency after KEAP1 loss.\n\nValidation and deadline assessment: none new. Existing validation for USP7/TP53, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI-high, NFE2L2/KEAP1, STAT3/PTEN overall and TP53-loss subgroup, MDM2/CDKN2A overall and TP53-intact and low-9p21 strata, and SMARCA4 interaction by ARID1A remains informative. All independent intervals are within-study validation intervals and account for the maximum number of validation comparisons, not external replication.\n\nSupported core findings. 1) TP53 non-loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss: discovery +0.802 [0.782, 0.822], independent validation +0.811 [0.782, 0.841]. This is among the largest accepted effects and remains large in many internal strata, including adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, high and lower screen quality, KY and non-KY library, batch A, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, aneuploidy strata, and high research_signature_a +0.823 [0.788, 0.857]. 2) SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803], validation +0.805 [0.774, 0.836]. This synthetic-lethality-like association is robust across ARID1A strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch, STK11-loss cells, KY and non-KY library, and high research_signature_a +0.785 [0.750, 0.819]. 3) MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: discovery +0.790 [0.760, 0.819], validation +0.790 [0.736, 0.843]. It is robust across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, and high research_signature_a +0.799 [0.739, 0.860], though some strata have small exposed counts. 4) KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, after correcting the registered direction: discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816], validation +0.802 [0.775, 0.829]. It is robust across TP53, lineage, STK11, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, and high research_signature_a +0.798 [0.758, 0.837]. 5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery +0.267 [0.215, 0.319], validation +0.292 [0.213, 0.370]. The effect is moderate but reproducible and is amplified in TP53-loss cells: discovery +0.190 [0.085, 0.296], validation +0.442 [0.265, 0.619]. It remains positive in many technical and mutation strata, although batch-A validation crossed zero and remains unresolved. 6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: discovery +0.117 [0.082, 0.152], validation +0.114 [0.067, 0.161]. This is a smaller but internally robust association, strongest in TP53-intact cells, validated +0.159 [0.101, 0.218], and in low copy_number_9p21 cells, validated +0.110 [0.036, 0.184]. TP53 loss by itself is not supported as a simple MDM2 driver in the originally tested direction.\n\nContext-specific findings. The constructed research signatures modify two moderate axes but should not be interpreted as assigned biological pathways. For PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, high research_signature_a amplifies the association: high signature_a direct +0.604 [0.513, 0.695], extreme high signature_a +0.627 [0.500, 0.755], and the signature_a interaction +0.489 [0.385, 0.593]. High research_signature_c attenuates the PTEN effect: the reversed signature_c interaction is accepted at +0.163 [0.056, 0.270], with direct high signature_c +0.156 [0.071, 0.242] and low signature_c +0.319 [0.255, 0.384]. The completed signature_c by signature_a decomposition shows: high A low C +0.648 [0.548, 0.749]; high C high A +0.469 [0.253, 0.685] but only 20 exposed cells; low C low A +0.144 [0.080, 0.209]; high C low A +0.060 [-0.020, 0.140], rejected. High signature_b also attenuates: high signature_b direct +0.018 [-0.025, 0.061] rejected and low signature_b +0.392 [0.327, 0.457] accepted, with a reversed high-signature-b interaction +0.411 [0.333, 0.488]. Together, PTEN-STAT3 is most strongly expressed in high signature_a and low signature_b/signature_c contexts. For CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency, high research_signature_c concentrates the association: direct high signature_c +0.390 [0.304, 0.475], high C low A +0.334 [0.230, 0.437], high B high C +0.765 [0.692, 0.838], and high C low B +0.207 [0.107, 0.307]. Iteration 22/25, stage explore, attempt 1.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.
