The final synthesis therefore rests on the accepted discovery claims plus previously returned validation comparisons. For direction -1 dependency-score claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed predictor is associated with a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score; for the accepted NFE2L2/KEAP1 direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate encodes the reversed phenotype direction accepted in this study, interpreted here as a weaker NFE2L2 dependency association after KEAP1 loss. I use approximately 0.10 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical benchmark because the outcomes are centered negative CRISPR scores and a strict 10% relative criterion is not directly interpretable on the dependency scale. SUPPORTED FINDINGS. The strongest accepted axes are TP53 status for USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high for WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2 dependency in the accepted reversed direction. USP7: TP53 non-loss versus loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, discovery +0.802 [0.782,0.822] and independent validation +0.811 [0.782,0.841]; the association remains very large across adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, screen-quality strata, library strata, batch A, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, aneuploidy strata, direct research_signature_a strata, high EMT, and TP53-intact/KEAP1-loss contexts. SMARCA2: SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, discovery +0.784 [0.765,0.803] and validation +0.805 [0.774,0.836]; this synthetic-lethality-like association is retained across ARID1A strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch, STK11 loss, library strata, research_signature_a strata, high stemness, and SMARCA4 by ARID1A interaction tests. WRN: MSI-high versus non-MSI is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, discovery +0.790 [0.760,0.819] and validation +0.790 [0.736,0.843]; it is stable across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, high hypoxia, research_signature_a strata, and direct high/low signature contexts, although some exposed cells are small. NFE2L2: KEAP1 loss is associated with a very large accepted effect in the reversed direction, discovery +0.796 [0.776,0.816] and validation +0.802 [0.775,0.829]; the association persists across TP53, lineage, STK11, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, high IFN-gamma context, and research_signature_a strata. The moderate but reproducible PTEN-loss STAT3 axis is accepted: overall discovery +0.267 [0.215,0.319] and validation +0.292 [0.213,0.370], with apparent amplification in TP53-loss cells, discovery +0.190 [0.085,0.296] and validation +0.442 [0.265,0.619]. Its magnitude is context-modified by constructed signatures: direct high research_signature_a +0.604 [0.513,0.695] and the high-signature_a interaction +0.489 [0.385,0.593] indicate amplification; direct high research_signature_c +0.156 [0.071,0.242] is smaller, high research_signature_c low research_signature_a +0.060 [-0.020,0.140] is rejected as non-robust, and high research_signature_b direct +0.018 [-0.025,0.061] is rejected while low research_signature_b +0.392 [0.327,0.457] and the reversed high-signature_b interaction +0.411 [0.333,0.488] are accepted. Thus PTEN-STAT3 is most clearly expressed in high research_signature_a with low research_signature_b/signature_c contexts, although signature labels are constructed assays without assigned biological pathway meaning. The CDKN2A-loss MDM2 axis is also accepted but smaller: overall discovery +0.117 [0.082,0.152] and validation +0.114 [0.067,0.161]. It is strongest and validated in TP53-intact cells, discovery +0.118 [0.079,0.158] and validation +0.159 [0.101,0.218], and is also accepted in cells with low copy_number_9p21, discovery +0.135 [0.091,0.179] and validation +0.110 [0.036,0.184]. Context decomposition shows a signature_c concentration: direct high research_signature_c +0.390 [0.304,0.475], high signature_b with high signature_c +0.765 [0.692,0.838], high signature_c with low signature_b +0.207 [0.107,0.307], and high signature_c with low signature_a +0.334 [0.230,0.437]. By contrast, high research_signature_a with low signature_c is null and rejected, -0.010 [-0.057,0.038]. The completed low signature_c low signature_a cell is near null and rejected, +0.0066 [-0.0191,0.0324]. Direct high research_signature_a CDKN2A-MDM2 is accepted at +0.163 [0.091,0.236], but this is not interpreted as signature_a-specific because the corresponding high-signature_a interaction was rejected; direct low research_signature_a +0.096 [0.057,0.134] falls below the practical benchmark and is rejected as independently meaningful. High and low MYC RNA strata are similar, +0.111 [0.060,0.163] and +0.104 [0.047,0.161], supporting a broadly retained CDKN2A-MDM2 association rather than clear MYC-expression modification. ROBUSTNESS AND CAVEATS. The core axes remain very large across technical and biological strata, including high and low constructed signature_a and high EMT, stemness, hypoxia, and IFN-gamma contexts. However, some strata have small exposed counts, especially high hypoxia MSI-high WRN with only 31 exposed cells, and the PTEN-STAT3 batch_A subgroup remains unresolved because validation +0.159 [-0.018,0.335] crosses zero despite positive discovery. These uncertainties affect subgroup precision, not the core accepted associations. NEGATIVE OR BOUNDED FINDINGS. The final synthesis therefore rests on the accepted discovery claims plus previously returned validation comparisons. For direction -1 dependency-score claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed predictor is associated with a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score; for the accepted NFE2L2/KEAP1 direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate encodes the reversed phenotype direction accepted in this study, interpreted here as a weaker NFE2L2 dependency association after KEAP1 loss. I use approximately 0.10 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical benchmark because the outcomes are centered negative CRISPR scores and a strict 10% relative criterion is not directly interpretable on the dependency scale. SUPPORTED FINDINGS. The strongest accepted axes are TP53 status for USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high for WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2 dependency in the accepted reversed direction. USP7: TP53 non-loss versus loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, discovery +0.802 [0.782,0.822] and independent validation +0.811 [0.782,0.841]; the association remains very large across adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, screen-quality strata, library strata, batch A, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, aneuploidy strata, direct research_signature_a strata, high EMT, and TP53-intact/KEAP1-loss contexts. SMARCA2: SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, discovery +0.784 [0.765,0.803] and validation +0.805 [0.774,0.836]; this synthetic-lethality-like association is retained across ARID1A strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch, STK11 loss, library strata, research_signature_a strata, high stemness, and SMARCA4 by ARID1A interaction tests. WRN: MSI-high versus non-MSI is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, discovery +0.790 [0.760,0.819] and validation +0.790 [0.736,0.843]; it is stable across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, high hypoxia, research_signature_a strata, and direct high/low signature contexts, although some exposed cells are small. NFE2L2: KEAP1 loss is associated with a very large accepted effect in the reversed direction, discovery +0.796 [0.776,0.816] and validation +0.802 [0.775,0.829]; the association persists across TP53, lineage, STK11, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, high IFN-gamma context, and research_signature_a strata. The moderate but reproducible PTEN-loss STAT3 axis is accepted: overall discovery +0.267 [0.215,0.319] and validation +0.292 [0.213,0.370], with apparent amplification in TP53-loss cells, discovery +0.190 [0.085,0.296] and validation +0.442 [0.265,0.619]. Its magnitude is context-modified by constructed signatures: direct high research_signature_a +0.604 [0.513,0.695] and the high-signature_a interaction +0.489 [0.385,0.593] indicate amplification; direct high research_signature_c +0.156 [0.071,0.242] is smaller, high research_signature_c low research_signature_a +0.060 [-0.020,0.140] is rejected as non-robust, and high research_signature_b direct +0.018 [-0.025,0.061] is rejected while low research_signature_b +0.392 [0.327,0.457] and the reversed high-signature_b interaction +0.411 [0.333,0.488] are accepted. Thus PTEN-STAT3 is most clearly expressed in high research_signature_a with low research_signature_b/signature_c contexts, although signature labels are constructed assays without assigned biological pathway meaning. The CDKN2A-loss MDM2 axis is also accepted but smaller: overall discovery +0.117 [0.082,0.152] and validation +0.114 [0.067,0.161]. It is strongest and validated in TP53-intact cells, discovery +0.118 [0.079,0.158] and validation +0.159 [0.101,0.218], and is also accepted in cells with low copy_number_9p21, discovery +0.135 [0.091,0.179] and validation +0.110 [0.036,0.184]. Context decomposition shows a signature_c concentration: direct high research_signature_c +0.390 [0.304,0.475], high signature_b with high signature_c +0.765 [0.692,0.838], high signature_c with low signature_b +0.207 [0.107,0.307], and high signature_c with low signature_a +0.334 [0.230,0.437]. By contrast, high research_signature_a with low signature_c is null and rejected, -0.010 [-0.057,0.038]. The completed low signature_c low signature_a cell is near null and rejected, +0.0066 [-0.0191,0.0324]. Direct high research_signature_a CDKN2A-MDM2 is accepted at +0.163 [0.091,0.236], but this is not interpreted as signature_a-specific because the corresponding high-signature_a interaction was rejected; direct low research_signature_a +0.096 [0.057,0.134] falls below the practical benchmark and is rejected as independently meaningful. High and low MYC RNA strata are similar, +0.111 [0.060,0.163] and +0.104 [0.047,0.161], supporting a broadly retained CDKN2A-MDM2 association rather than clear MYC-expression modification. ROBUSTNESS AND CAVEATS. The core axes remain very large across technical and biological strata, including high and low constructed signature_a and high EMT, stemness, hypoxia, and IFN-gamma contexts. However, some strata have small exposed counts, especially high hypoxia MSI-high WRN with only 31 exposed cells, and the PTEN-STAT3 batch_A subgroup remains unresolved because validation +0.159 [-0.018,0.335] crosses zero despite positive discovery. These uncertainties affect subgroup precision, not the core accepted associations. NEGATIVE OR BOUNDED FINDINGS. H295 gives the complementary low-hypoxia direct stratum at +0.2875 [0.2133, 0.3618]; accept and close. record.narrative: No new validation was released and no response-deadline assessments are pending, and the voluntary independent validation budget is exhausted. I close the three remaining untested formal interaction proposals H305-H307 as unresolved rather than leaving them active, because the analysis and validation budgets are not available to address them and further unstructured threshold stratification has low expected value. This synthesis is based on the accepted discovery claims in the supplied dataset plus previously returned within-study validation comparisons. For direction -1 dependency-score claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed predictor is associated with a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score. For the accepted NFE2L2/KEAP1 claims in the direction +1 reversed framework, a positive signed estimate encodes less negative NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. weaker dependency after KEAP1 loss. I use about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical meaningfulness benchmark because the outcomes are centered negative CRISPR scores and a relative 10 percent rule is not directly interpretable on this scale. SUPPORTED FINDINGS. Four very large measured dependency axes are robust in this dataset. First, TP53 non-loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss, discovery estimate about +0.802 [0.782,0.822] and independent validation estimate about +0.811 [0.782,0.841]; this remains very large across adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, library strata, batch A, screen-quality strata, aneuploidy strata, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, high EMT context, high research_signature_a, low research_signature_a, low serum, and other accepted contexts. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4 non-loss, discovery estimate about +0.784 [0.765,0.803] and validation estimate about +0.805 [0.774,0.836]; this synthetic-lethality-like association is retained across ARID1A-loss strata, ARID1A-non-loss strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, batch A, library strata, STK11-loss cells, high stemness, higher ploidy, high research_signature_a, and low research_signature_a. The corresponding ARID1A, TP53, lineage, signature_b, signature_c, and marker interaction tests do not support additional effect modification. Third, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency than non-MSI-high, discovery estimate about +0.790 [0.760,0.819] and validation estimate about +0.790 [0.736,0.843]; this is retained across mutation-burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, high hypoxia, research_signature_a strata, and direct high/low signature contexts, though some exposed cells are small. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with much less negative NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency in the accepted reversed direction, with discovery estimate about +0.796 [0.776,0.816] and validation estimate about +0.802 [0.775,0.829]; this association persists across TP53 strata, lineage, STK11-loss cells, library, culture, batch A, screen quality, high IFN-gamma context, and research_signature_a strata. Two moderate axes are also supported. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, overall discovery estimate about +0.267 [0.215,0.319] and validation estimate about +0.292 [0.213,0.370]. It is accepted in TP53-intact cells about +0.287 [0.227,0.347], and in TP53-loss cells about +0.190 [0.085,0.296] with validation about +0.442 [0.265,0.619]. It is accepted across high and low hypoxia direct strata, about +0.250 [0.149,0.352] and +0.288 [0.213,0.362], across screen-quality strata, culture, lineage, kras strata, pik3ca strata, and many constructed-signature contexts. Its magnitude is strongly context-modified: high research_signature_a direct estimate about +0.604 [0.513,0.695], high research_signature_a interaction estimate about +0.489 [0.385,0.593], high research_signature_a with low research_signature_c about +0.648 [0.548,0.749], and high research_signature_a with high research_signature_c about +0.469 [0.253,0.685], whereas high research_signature_b direct estimate about +0.018 [-0.025,0.061] is rejected; low research_signature_b direct estimate about +0.392 [0.327,0.457] and the corresponding reversed interaction about +0.411 [0.333,0.488] are accepted. High research_signature_c direct estimate about +0.156 [0.071,0.242] is accepted but smaller, and high research_signature_c with low research_signature_a about +0.060 [-0.020,0.140] is rejected as not robustly meaningful. Thus PTEN-STAT3 is most clearly expressed in high research_signature_a and lower research_signature_b/research_signature_c contexts, but these signature labels are constructed assays and not assigned biological pathways. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, overall discovery estimate about +0.117 [0.082,0.152] and validation estimate about +0.114 [0.067,0.161]. It is accepted in TP53-intact cells about +0.118 [0.079,0.158] with validation about +0.159 [0.101,0.218], in 9p21-low cells about +0.135 [0.091,0.179] with validation about +0.110 [0.036,0.184], in TP53-loss 9p21-low cells about +0.204 [0.106,0.303], in TP53-loss/MTAP-non-loss cells about +0.100 [0.018,0.181], and in high research_signature_c contexts about +0.390 [0.304,0.475], with the high signature_c interaction about +0.388 [0.300,0.476]. The strongest signature-cell estimates are high research_signature_b with high research_signature_c about +0.765 [0.692,0.838] and high signature_c with low signature_a about +0.334 [0.230,0.437]. By contrast, high research_signature_a with low research_signature_c is null about -0.010 [-0.057,0.038], low signature_c low signature_a is null about +0.007 [-0.019,0.032], and direct low research_signature_a about +0.096 [0.057,0.134] falls just below the practical benchmark and is not accepted as independently meaningful. Direct high and low MYC-RNA strata are similar, about +0.111 [0.060,0.163] and +0.104 [0.047,0.161], supporting a broadly retained CDKN2A-MDM2 association rather than a clear MYC-expression modification; however, the formal MYC interaction H306 was not tested and is now closed. NEGATIVE OR BOUNDED FINDINGS. Driver-matched dependency effects are not supported in this dataset: KRAS mutation does not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not predict EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict ERBB2 dependency; EGFR amplification also did not predict KRAS or TMED10 dependency in broad tests. The originally registered TP53-loss MDM2 direction is rejected, and MTAP loss does not provide a robust independent MDM2 signal after conditioning on CDKN2A. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 among the tested dependency axes; it is rejected for MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, BRAF, and most specificity tests, with DHX9 and RIT1 tests under high screen quality also rejected as small or imprecise. CDKN2A loss is selective for MDM2 and is rejected as spilling over to USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 dependency. Research markers D, E, and F behave largely as low-information or negative-control strata, and research signatures are constructed standardized assays without assigned gene or pathway meaning. Some nominally detected small effects, such as TP53 loss for KIF18A about +0.021 [0.001,0.040] and RB1 loss for POLR2A about +0.025 [-0.001,0.051], are rejected as not practically meaningful. Many formal interaction tests for lineage, TP53, ARID1A, MTAP, batch, library, markers, MYC amplification, and other technical or biological contexts are rejected or unresolved, generally because intervals are wide, cells are small, or effects are too small for the dependency scale. Screen-quality eligibility may be collider-like because screen performance can depend on cell state and genotype, so high-quality-screen nulls are bounded evidence rather than proof of absence. UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY. The batch-A PTEN-loss STAT3 subgroup remains unresolved because validation estimate about +0.159 [-0.018,0.335] crosses zero despite positive discovery. Several signature and TP53-stratum decompositions involve small exposed cells, especially high research_signature contexts and some high-hypoxia MSI-high WRN cells. The formal hypoxia interaction H305, MYC-RNA interaction H306, and STK11-loss SMARCA4-SMARCA2 interaction H307 remain untested and are closed. Deferred technical interactions, such as library and batch modifications, also remain unresolved. All validation here is internal to the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset and should not be interpreted as external replication, causality, or clinical generalizability. MULTIP LICITY is another limitation: many subgroup and signature tests were performed, so the strongest accepted patterns should be regarded as internally consistent measured associations that would benefit from pre-specified external confirmation. MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS. Further within-dataset threshold stratification is unlikely to change the main conclusions. The highest-value next step is adequately powered, pre-specified external validation of the two context-sensitive moderate axes: PTEN-loss STAT3 in high research_signature_a and lower research_signature_b/c contexts, and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 in high research_signature_c and TP53-intact or 9p21-low contexts. A targeted validation design should pre-specify these interaction hypotheses rather than perform additional exploratory thresholds. To move from association to mechanism or therapeutic relevance, experimental perturbation of TP53, USP7, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, MSI/WRN biology, KEAP1/NFE2L2 signaling, PTEN/STAT3, and CDKN2A/9p21/MDM2 biology would be needed. The four very large dependency axes and the two moderate axes are the main scientifically meaningful findings supported by this dataset.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

This is a robust moderate association, well above a practical dependency-score threshold and consistent with the accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 axis; accept and close, while noting that high-hypoxia cells are only 75 exposed and the hypoxia assay is constructed. H295 gives the complementary low-hypoxia direct stratum at +0.2875 [0.2133, 0.3618]; accept and close. Together H288 and H295 suggest that the PTEN-loss STAT3 association persists across hypoxia strata, but they are not formal evidence against interaction because the direct strata are separately estimated. H296 tests the accepted SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 axis at higher ploidy and gives +0.7619 [0.7263, 0.7976]; accept and close as a strong retained synthetic-lethality-like association. H297 tests the accepted TP53 non-loss USP7 axis under lower serum and gives +0.8047 [0.7743, 0.8351]; accept and close as a very large retained association. H294 tests whether lineage subtype modifies CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency and gives -0.0098 [-0.0878, 0.0682], a near-null interval crossing zero; reject and close. This does not overturn the accepted overall CDKN2A-MDM2 association, but it does not support adenocarcinoma-specific modification. The remaining new results are specificity or residual-context tests and are mostly negative. H298 STK11-loss EGFR dependency +0.0021 [-0.0176, 0.0217] and H299 STK11-loss STAT3 dependency +0.0145 [-0.0137, 0.0427] are small and null; reject and close. H300 RB1-loss POLR2A dependency +0.0249 [-0.0009, 0.0507] is borderline near a nominal 10 percent of a typical dependency baseline but is below a more conservative practical benchmark and its interval is not robustly positive; reject and close. H301 RB1-loss RPL11 dependency -0.0204 [-0.0478, 0.0070] is small, imprecise, and in the unexpected signed direction; reject and close. H302 PTEN-loss DHX9 dependency under high screen quality -0.0259 [-0.0564, 0.0047] is small, opposite-signed, and crosses zero; reject and close. H303 PTEN-loss RIT1 dependency under high screen quality +0.0292 [-0.0015, 0.0599] is borderline small and imprecise; reject as not a meaningful supported specificity. H304 TP53-loss POLR2A dependency under high screen quality +0.0107 [-0.0159, 0.0374] is null; reject and close. A critical caveat is that screen-quality eligibility may act as a collider-like filter because screening performance can depend on cell state and genotype, so nulls in H302-H304 are bounded evidence, not proof of no PTEN or TP53 effects. For direction -1 dependency-score claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed predictor is associated with a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score. For the accepted NFE2L2/KEAP1 claims in the direction +1 reversed framework, a positive signed estimate encodes less negative NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. weaker dependency after KEAP1 loss. I use about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical meaningfulness benchmark because the outcomes are centered negative CRISPR scores and a relative 10 percent rule is not directly interpretable on this scale. record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this corrected explore stage registers only within-dataset comparisons and avoids parent/refinement links to prevent the prior motivating-result error. The stable accepted framework remains four very large measured axes and two moderate axes; these proposals target unresolved formal context effects and remaining driver/specificity checks rather than additional low-value threshold strata. A practical benchmark of about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units is used because the outcomes are centered negative CRISPR scores and a relative 10% rule is not directly interpretable. For direction -1 mean differences, positive signed estimates mean the exposed predictor is associated with more negative, stronger dependency. For direction -1 interactions, positive signed estimates mean the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the registered subgroup than in its complement within the same eligibility. For the KEAP1/NFE2L2 direction +1 claim, positive signed estimates encode the accepted reversed weaker-dependency direction. The registered comparisons are: whether the PTEN-loss STAT3 association is modified by high hypoxia within TP53-intact cells; whether the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association is modified by high MYC RNA within TP53-intact cells; whether the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 association is modified by STK11 loss within adenocarcinoma; whether TP53 non-loss USP7 dependency is modified by CDKN2A loss or KEAP1 loss; whether MSI-high WRN dependency is modified by TP53 loss; whether KRAS mutation has an unexpected STAT3 specificity; and whether the KEAP1/NFE2L2 reversed association is modified by STK11 loss. The prior expectation is mostly uncertain or null for many interactions because direct strata are similar, but any robust absolute interaction or mean difference above the practical benchmark would identify scientifically meaningful context dependence. All statements remain associations in the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset, not causal, clinical, or externally generalizable claims.

Iteration 23/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new discovery batch tests formal context and lineage-subtype interactions for the main supported dependency axes, plus one driver-specificity residual test. Using the same practical benchmark as earlier in the run, a scientifically meaningful interaction for these dependency-score contrasts should be both directionally consistent and, after sign coding, have a point estimate above about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units with an interval that excludes zero. None of the new results satisfies that standard. H308 tests whether high hypoxia modifies the PTEN-loss STAT3 association within TP53-intact cells; signed estimate -0.021 [-0.154, 0.112] is small, crosses zero, and does not support hypoxia-specific modification. H309 tests MYC-RNA modification of CDKN2A-loss MDM2 within TP53-intact cells: -0.0004 [-0.079, 0.078] is essentially null and does not support MYC-expression context dependence. H310 tests STK11-loss modification of the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 association within adenocarcinoma: +0.020 [-0.034, 0.075] is small and not zero-excluding; reject. H311 tests CDKN2A-loss modification of TP53 non-loss USP7 dependency: +0.007 [-0.039, 0.054] is null; reject. H312 tests TP53-loss modification of MSI-high WRN dependency: +0.053 [-0.022, 0.127] is positive but below the practical benchmark and crosses zero; the exposed TP53-loss MSI-high cell is only 24, so the interval is imprecise. This is not evidence for a meaningful TP53-loss context interaction, though it does not prove absence. H313 tests KEAP1-loss modification of TP53 non-loss USP7 dependency: -0.010 [-0.056, 0.036] is null; reject. H314 tests KRAS mutation as an unexpected STAT3 predictor: -0.018 [-0.042, 0.007] is small, opposite the registered direction, and crosses zero; it does not support driver-matched STAT3 specificity. H315 tests STK11-loss modification of the reversed KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 association: -0.026 [-0.079, 0.026] is small and null in the direction-plus framework; reject. The formal lineage-subtype robustness interactions are likewise unsupported: H35 SMARCA4-SMARCA2 by adenocarcinoma -0.028 [-0.076, 0.020]; H36 TP53-USP7 by adenocarcinoma -0.010 [-0.053, 0.033]; H138 MSI-WRN by adenocarcinoma -0.021 [-0.085, 0.042]; H139 reversed KEAP1-NFE2L2 by adenocarcinoma -0.012 [-0.057, 0.033]. These are not rejected as proof that lineage subtype has no effect; they are rejected as unsupported context-specific differences in this dataset. Their main value is to show that the large main effects do not depend solely on one subtype. A critical caution is that several context tests have small exposed cells and many such tests have been run, so nulls are bounded, not definitive. No further voluntary validation is possible; all conclusions remain associations within the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so this explore stage registers only new within-dataset hypotheses. The accepted framework already contains four very large associations and two moderate associations, but several formally important context interactions remain untested or were only tested through direct strata. These proposals prioritize the highest-value remaining comparisons: (1) formal interaction tests by research signature A for USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, and the accepted reversed NFE2L2 association, completing the signature-modification evidence already obtained for signatures B and C; (2) a biologically plausible IFN-gamma context test for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency; (3) a hypoxia context test for CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency restricted to TP53-intact cells, where the MDM2-p53 axis is most directly relevant; and (4) low-Cas9 activity attenuation tests for the three robust axes with adequately exposed cells. For direction -1 mean-difference claims, a raw negative contrast means the exposed predictor has a more negative score, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 NFE2L2 claims, a raw positive contrast means less negative scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency. For interaction claims, anticipated_direction is the raw contrast in the named subgroup minus its complement before applying claim direction. Thus low-Cas9 attenuation of the large TP53/SMARCA4 effects is encoded as raw interaction +1 because the low-Cas9 raw contrast is expected to be less negative than in higher-Cas9 cells, whereas low-Cas9 attenuation of the accepted reversed NFE2L2 effect is encoded as raw interaction -1 because the low-Cas9 raw weaker-dependency contrast is expected to be smaller than in higher-Cas9 cells. The IFN-gamma test expects raw interaction -1 because stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency would make the raw contrast more negative in high IFN. Research signatures and IFN/hypoxia scores are constructed assays or pathway-like scores, so any accepted interaction supports measured context dependence, not external biological mechanism. Missing Cas9 activity values may reduce cells and some Cas9 interactions could fail minimum cell counts; if that occurs the result is bounded rather than informative. All claims remain associations in the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset and are not causal, clinical, or externally generalizable.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

I request the nine active claims registered by the last explore stage because they complete formal context-interaction evidence for the main supported axes: H316-H319 formally test whether research signature A modifies the large USP7/TP53, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI-high, and reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1 associations, complementing direct signature-A strata already obtained and the previously rejected signature-B/C interaction tests. H320 tests IFN-gamma-signature modification of the accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 association, and H321 tests hypoxia modification of the accepted CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association restricted to TP53-intact cells. H322-H324 test whether low Cas9 activity attenuates the largest associations, a technical-diagnostic context because lower CRISPR editing could compress observed dependency contrasts. I add three deferred specificity tests that close missing predictor-outcome cells in the specificity framework: H134 and H135 test whether SMARCA4 loss or KEAP1 loss cross-over to WRN dependency, and H293 tests whether TP53 loss cross-over to POLR2A dependency. These are associations in the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset only; biological meaning of constructed signatures and pathway scores remains unassigned. Direction signs are already encoded: for direction -1 mean differences, positive signed estimates indicate stronger dependency in the exposed predictor; for direction -1 interactions, positive signed estimates indicate the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative inside the named subgroup than in its complement. Conclusions below are associations in the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset, not causal claims or externally generalizable therapeutic claims.\n\nPractical framework: dependency scores are more negative when dependency is stronger. Overall H94 is +0.267 [0.215,0.319]; validation +0.292 [0.213,0.370]. This is accepted in TP53-intact cells and TP53-loss cells, across high and low hypoxia direct strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, KRAS strata, PIK3CA strata, and many constructed-signature contexts. These signature labels are constructed assays with no assigned pathway, so the interpretation is measured context dependence, not biological pathway causation.\n6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Overall H154 is +0.117 [0.082,0.152]; validation +0.114 [0.067,0.161]. It is accepted in TP53-intact cells (+0.118 [0.079,0.158]; validation +0.159 [0.101,0.218]), TP53-loss cells (+0.111 [0.035,0.186]), 9p21-low cells (+0.135 [0.091,0.179]; validation +0.110 [0.036,0.184]), TP53-loss/9p21-low cells (+0.204 [0.106,0.303]), TP53-loss/MTAP-non-loss cells (+0.100 [0.018,0.181]), and high research signature C contexts (direct +0.390 [0.304,0.475]; interaction +0.388 [0.300,0.476]). Stronger nested signature estimates include high signature B plus high signature C about +0.765 [0.692,0.838] and high signature C with high signature A about +0.490 [0.340,0.641]. By contrast, high signature A with low signature C is null about -0.010 [-0.057,0.038] and low signature C with low signature A is near null. MYC RNA high and low strata are similar, supporting broad retention rather than clear MYC-expression modification, although the formal MYC interaction remains untested and closed.\n\nSpecificity and negative findings:\nDriver-matched dependency effects are not supported. KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful difference in KRAS dependency (+0.014 [-0.004,0.031] signed; raw small). BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful difference in BRAF dependency (-0.017 [-0.045,0.012] signed). Several signature and TP53-stratum estimates involve small cells, especially high signature contexts and TP53-loss MSI-high WRN. Formal interactions H305-H307 and deferred technical interactions remain untested or unresolved because analysis/validation capacity is exhausted. The dataset is limited to lung cell lines and constructed assays; biological mechanism, clinical relevance, and generalizability are not established.\n\nMost informative next analysis:\nThe highest value next step is adequate powered pre-specified external validation of the context-sensitive moderate axes: PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in high research signature A and lower research signature B or C contexts, and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency in high research signature C and/or 9p21-low/TP53-intact contexts. External confirmation should also cover the four large axes. Mechanistic work would require perturbation of TP53-USP7, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, MSI/WRN, KEAP1/NFE2L2, PTEN/STAT3, and CDKN2A/9p21/MDM2 biology rather than additional exploratory thresholds."}}

record.narrative: This batch tests formal context-interaction hypotheses for the robust dependency axes, two predictor-outcome specificity residuals, and one deferred TP53-POLR2A cross-test. I used the same conservative benchmark as throughout the run: a context interaction or cross-predictor effect is scientifically meaningful only if the signed estimate is practically substantial, generally above about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, and the 95% interval excludes zero; small interval-crossing estimates are treated as unsupported rather than proof of absence, especially in small cells. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction -1 interactions, a positive signed interaction means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the named subgroup than in its complement. The accepted reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1 claims use direction +1, where positive signed estimates encode less negative NFE2L2 scores after KEAP1 loss, i.e. weaker measured dependency. H316-H319 test whether research signature A modifies the large USP7-TP53, SMARCA2-SMARCA4, WRN-MSI-high, and reversed NFE2L2-KEAP1 associations. All four signed interaction estimates are small and interval-crossing: H316 +0.030 [-0.011, 0.072], H317 +0.001 [-0.040, 0.043], H318 +0.012 [-0.057, 0.081], and H319 +0.002 [-0.044, 0.048]. These do not support an additional signature-A-specific modification beyond the already accepted direct signature-A strata; I reject them as unsupported context differences and close these investigations, noting that bounded uncertainty remains, especially where subgroup cells are modest. H320 is the only new result meeting the practical and inferential standard. The high IFN-gamma interaction for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is signed +0.221 [0.104, 0.338], excludes zero, and is well above the practical benchmark. Because this is a direction -1 interaction, the positive signed estimate means the raw PTEN-loss contrast is more negative, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency, in high IFN-gamma cells than in lower IFN-gamma cells. I accept H320 as a measured context-dependent association in this dataset, but not as evidence for causal IFN signaling or external generalizability. I keep the investigation active because direct high IFN and lower IFN mean differences should be estimated to quantify the absolute context-specific effect rather than only the interaction. H321 tests hypoxia modification of CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency within TP53-intact cells: signed -0.030 [-0.116, 0.056]. Conclusions below are associations in the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset, not causal claims or externally generalizable therapeutic claims.\n\nPractical framework: dependency scores are more negative when dependency is stronger. Signed estimates for direction -1 mean claims are positive when the exposed group has a more negative score. Signed estimates for direction -1 interactions are positive when the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative inside the subgroup than in its complement. The accepted NFE2L2/KEAP1 claims use direction +1 and positive signed estimates encode less negative NFE2L2 scores after KEAP1 loss, i.e. weaker measured dependency. Because CRISPR scores are centered negative values and not zero-based biological quantities, the generic 10% relative rule is not very informative here. I used about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical benchmark for scientifically meaningful differences, while also requiring interval exclusion of zero and consistency.\n\nSupported large axes:\n1) TP53 non-loss versus TP53 loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency. H6 shows +0.802 [0.782,0.822]; H6 validation shows +0.811 [0.782,0.841]. The difference is far above the practical benchmark and is robust across adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, library strata, screen-quality strata, aneuploidy strata, MYC amplification, KEAP1 loss, high EMT, high and low research signature A, low serum media, and other accepted contexts. Formal interactions tested in the ledger generally do not support additional meaningful effect modification.\n2) SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H7 shows +0.784 [0.765,0.803]; validation +0.805 [0.774,0.836]. This synthetic-lethality-like association is retained across ARID1A-loss and non-loss cells, lineage subtype, culture, screen quality, batch, library, STK11 loss, stemness, ploidy, and research signature A contexts. ARID1A-loss versus non-loss does not support a separate independent effect, and the main interaction tests are unsupported or bounded nulls.\n3) MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. H9 shows +0.790 [0.760,0.819]; validation +0.790 [0.736,0.843]. Robustness is seen across mutation burden thresholds, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen quality, BRCA2-loss exclusion, hypoxia, and research signature A contexts. Some high-strata exposed cells are small, so those specific contexts are robust in direction but less precise.\n4) KEAP1 loss is associated with less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency under the accepted reversed framing. H13 shows +0.796 [0.776,0.816]; validation +0.802 [0.775,0.829]. This persists across TP53 strata, lineage, STK11-loss cells, library, culture, batch, screen quality, high IFN gamma, and signature A strata. The original direction -1 H10 estimate was the negative of the accepted effect and is correctly rejected in that direction.\n\nSupported moderate axes:\n5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Overall H94 is +0.267 [0.215,0.319]; validation +0.292 [0.213,0.370]. This is accepted in TP53-intact cells and TP53-loss cells, across high and low hypoxia direct strata, lineage, culture, screen quality, KRAS strata, PIK3CA strata, and many constructed-signature contexts. The effect is context dependent: high research signature A direct estimate is about +0.604 [0.513,0.695], high signature A interaction about +0.489 [0.385,0.593], high signature A with low signature C about +0.648 [0.548,0.749], and high signature A with high signature C about +0.469 [0.253,0.685]. High signature B direct estimate is not meaningful, about +0.018 [-0.025,0.061], while low signature B direct estimate is about +0.392 [0.327,0.457] and the corresponding interaction is about +0.411 [0.333,0.488]. High signature C direct estimate is smaller but accepted, about +0.156 [0.071,0.242]. These signature labels are constructed assays with no assigned pathway, so the interpretation is measured context dependence, not biological pathway causation.\n6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Overall H154 is +0.117 [0.082,0.152]; validation +0.114 [0.067,0.161]. It is accepted in TP53-intact cells (+0.118 [0.079,0.158]; validation +0.159 [0.101,0.218]), TP53-loss cells (+0.111 [0.035,0.186]), 9p21-low cells (+0.135 [0.091,0.179]; validation +0.110 [0.036,0.184]), TP53-loss/9p21-low cells (+0.204 [0.106,0.303]), TP53-loss/MTAP-non-loss cells (+0.100 [0.018,0.181]), and high research signature C contexts (direct +0.390 [0.304,0.475]; interaction +0.388 [0.300,0.476]). Stronger nested signature estimates include high signature B plus high signature C about +0.765 [0.692,0.838] and high signature C with high signature A about +0.490 [0.340,0.641]. By contrast, high signature A with low signature C is null about -0.010 [-0.057,0.038] and low signature C with low signature A is near null. MYC RNA high and low strata are similar, supporting broad retention rather than clear MYC-expression modification, although the formal MYC interaction remains untested and closed.\n\nSpecificity and negative findings:\nDriver-matched dependency effects are not supported. KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful difference in KRAS dependency (+0.014 [-0.004,0.031] signed; raw small). BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful difference in BRAF dependency (-0.017 [-0.045,0.012] signed). EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful difference in EGFR dependency (+0.025 [-0.000,0.051] signed), and ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 dependency (+0.001 [-0.027,0.030] signed). EGFR amplification is also rejected for TMED10 and cross-driver checks, and EGFR amplification remains unresolved only in some deferred technical strata. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 among tested axes and is rejected or small for MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, BRAF, and most specificity checks; DHX9 and RIT1 high-quality-screen checks are also not supported. CDKN2A loss is selective for MDM2 and is rejected for USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2. MTAP loss does not provide a robust independent MDM2 signal after conditioning on CDKN2A. Research markers D, E, and F largely behave as low-information or negative-control strata. Some nominally detected very small effects, such as TP53 loss on KIF18A (+0.021 [0.001,0.040]) or RB1 loss on POLR2A (+0.025 [-0.001,0.051]), are rejected as not practically meaningful on the dependency-score scale.\n\nFormal context interactions are mostly bounded nulls. The main large axes do not show strong lineage-subtype modification, ARID1A modification of SMARCA2, CDKN2A or KEAP1 modification of USP7, TP53 modification of MSI-high WRN, MYC RNA modification of CDKN2A-MDM2, hypoxia modification of PTEN-STAT3, or STK11 modification of SMARCA4-SMARCA2 or KEAP1-NFE2L2. These are evidence that the registered context-specific differences are not supported in this dataset; they are not proof that such effects cannot exist. Some interaction tests have small exposed cells and the run contains many subgroup comparisons.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty:\nH99, PTEN-loss STAT3 in batch A, remains unresolved because validation estimate is about +0.159 [-0.018,0.335] and crosses zero despite positive discovery. Several signature and TP53-stratum estimates involve small cells, especially high signature contexts and TP53-loss MSI-high WRN. expectation
