The voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so the final scientific synthesis rests on the current discovery ledger plus previously returned validation comparisons. All conclusions below are measured associations in the supplied 2000-sample lung-cell-line CRISPR dependency dataset; they are not causal claims, therapeutic claims, or evidence of external generalizability. Direction convention: for direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For the accepted reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1 claims using direction +1, positive signed estimates mean less negative NFE2L2 scores after KEAP1 loss, i.e. weaker measured dependency. Because dependency scores are centered around negative values rather than zero-based biological quantities, the generic 10% relative rule is not highly informative; I used about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, interval exclusion of zero, and consistency as a conservative practical benchmark.\n\nSupported large, robust associations:\n1. TP53 non-loss versus TP53 loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency. H6 gives +0.802 [0.782, 0.822] (R6) and validation gives +0.811 [0.782, 0.841] (R50). This is far above the practical benchmark. The association is retained across adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma subsets, adherent culture, library strata, screen-quality strata, aneuploidy strata, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, EMT-high cells, high and low research-signature-A contexts, and low-serum media. Formal modifier tests generally do not support a large additional context-specific effect.\n2. SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H7 gives +0.784 [0.765, 0.803] (R7) and validation gives +0.805 [0.774, 0.836] (R13). This is a very large synthetic-lethality-like association in this dataset. It persists across ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-non-loss cells, lineage subtype, culture, screen-quality strata, batch, library, STK11-loss cells, stemness, ploidy, and signature-A contexts. ARID1A loss alone does not support a separate SMARCA2 effect, and formal interactions are unsupported or bounded nulls.\n3. MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. H9 gives +0.790 [0.760, 0.819] (R9) and validation gives +0.790 [0.736, 0.843] (R63). The effect is retained across mutation-burden strata, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen-quality strata, BRCA2-loss exclusion, hypoxia, and signature-A contexts. Some high-stratum exposed cells are small, so those contexts are directionally robust but less precise.\n4. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker measured NFE2L2 dependency, operationalized as less negative scores. The accepted reversed claim H13 gives +0.796 [0.776, 0.816] (R10) and validation gives +0.802 [0.775, 0.829] (R38). The effect is retained across TP53 strata, lineage, STK11-loss cells, library, culture, batch, screen-quality strata, IFN-gamma strata, and signature-A contexts. The original direction -1 claim H10 was correctly rejected because the raw effect is in the opposite direction under the dependency-score convention.\n\nSupported moderate associations:\n5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Overall H94 is +0.267 [0.215, 0.319] (R75) and validation is +0.292 [0.213, 0.370] (R76). The effect is present in TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells, across several lineage, culture, screen-quality, KRAS, PIK3CA, and hypoxia direct strata. It is also context dependent: it is larger in high research-signature-A contexts, smaller or null in high research-signature-B contexts, and smaller but still supported in high research-signature-C direct strata. The newly accepted interaction H320 shows that high IFN-gamma signature is associated with a stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 contrast relative to the complement: +0.221 [0.104, 0.338] (R290). Because H320 is direction -1, the positive signed interaction means the raw PTEN-loss contrast is more negative, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency, in high IFN-gamma cells. This is a measured context interaction in this dataset, not proof of causal IFN-gamma or JAK-STAT biology. Direct high and low IFN-gamma mean estimates were proposed but remain unquantified.\n6. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Overall H154 is +0.117 [0.082, 0.152] (R129) and validation is +0.114 [0.067, 0.161] (R141). The effect is present in TP53-intact cells, with internal validation also positive, and is present, though less precise, in TP53-loss cells. It is larger in 9p21-low contexts and in some nested signature contexts, especially high research-signature-C contexts and combinations involving high signature C with high signature A or B. In contrast, high signature A with low signature C is null, and low signature C with low signature A is near null. MYC RNA-expression high and low strata give broadly similar CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates, supporting broad retention rather than clear modification by measured MYC expression. MTAP loss does not provide a robust independent MDM2 signal after conditioning on CDKN2A loss.\n\nSpecificity and negative findings:\nThe most important negative finding is that driver-matched CRISPR dependency associations are not supported in this dataset. KRAS mutation does not show a practically meaningful KRAS dependency difference; BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful BRAF dependency difference; EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful EGFR dependency difference; and ERBB2 amplification does not show a meaningful ERBB2 dependency difference. Many EGFR and ERBB2 cross-checks, including TMED10 checks and mutation-restricted analyses, also do not support large associations. PTEN loss appears selective for STAT3 among the tested dependencies and is rejected or small for MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, BRAF, and most specificity checks. TP53 loss is selective for USP7 and does not support a practically meaningful MDM2 or STAT3 effect. SMARCA4 loss is selective for SMARCA2 and does not support WRN or USP7 cross-over effects. MSI-high is selective for WRN and does not support DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or POLR2A cross-over effects. KEAP1 loss is selective for the reversed NFE2L2 effect and does not support USP7, SMARCA2, or WRN cross-over effects. CDKN2A loss is selective for MDM2 and is rejected for USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2. MTAP loss remains negative for independent MDM2 effects after CDKN2A conditioning. Research markers D, E, and F largely behave as low-information or negative-control-like strata. Some nominally small effects, such as TP53-loss KIF18A or RB1-loss POLR2A, were rejected as not practically meaningful on the dependency-score scale.\n\nContext-interaction interpretation:\nThe four large associations are largely insensitive to measured technical and biological context modifiers. Many formal interactions for lineage subtype, ARID1A status, CDKN2A or KEAP1 status, TP53 status, MYC RNA expression, hypoxia, Cas9 activity, STK11 status, and research signature contexts were either unsupported or bounded nulls. By contrast, the moderate associations show the most meaningful context dependence. PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is modified by constructed signatures and by IFN-gamma signature. CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency is modified by 9p21 copy-number-like context and by research signatures, especially signature C-containing contexts. These signature contexts are constructed assays with no assigned biological pathway, so they should be treated as measured context labels, not biological mechanism claims.\n\nNegative findings are evidence against the registered context-specific or cross-predictor differences in this dataset, not proof of absence. Many analyses involve substantial multiplicity, small exposed cells in some strata, and possible collider-like effects from screen-quality eligibility. The largest associations are internally consistent and unusually strong, but causal interpretation remains uncertain.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty:\nH99 remains unresolved because PTEN-loss STAT3 in batch A was positive in discovery but validation crossed zero. Several signature-context estimates involve small cells. The direct high and low IFN-gamma mean differences for PTEN-loss STAT3, and the IFN-gamma specificity test for CDKN2A-loss MDM2, were registered but remain unquantified. Deferred technical interactions remain unresolved because analysis and validation capacity is exhausted. The dataset is limited to lung cell lines and constructed assays; biological mechanism, clinical relevance, and external generalizability are not established.\n\nMost informative next analysis:\nThe best next step is adequately powered, pre-specified external validation. It should test the four large axes and especially the moderate context-sensitive axes: PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in high research-signature-A, lower research-signature-B, and high IFN-gamma contexts; and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency in high research-signature-C and/or 9p21-low contexts, stratified by TP53 status where powered. If any within-dataset follow-up were possible, the most direct additions would be the proposed high/low IFN-gamma direct PTEN-STAT3 estimates and the CDKN2A-MDM2 IFN specificity test, but these should not be used for threshold mining. Ultimately, mechanistic perturbation of TP53-USP7, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, KEAP1-NFE2L2, PTEN-STAT3, and CDKN2A-9p21-MDM2 biology would be required to move from association toward causality."}}

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore stage registers only new within-dataset comparisons. The main unresolved scientific questions after H320 are: (1) quantify the absolute PTEN-loss STAT3 association in high versus lower IFN-gamma contexts rather than only the interaction, especially in TP53-intact cells where p53-MDM2/PTEN-related biology is most directly interpretable and cells are adequately powered; and (2) test whether the IFN-gamma context is specific to PTEN-STAT3 or extends to the larger TP53-USP7, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, and KEAP1-NFE2L2 associations, as well as to CDKN2A-MDM2. Existing active claims H325, H326, and H327 remain important: H325 and H326 provide direct all-TP53 high and lower IFN PTEN-STAT3 estimates, and H327 provides the formal CDKN2A-MDM2 IFN interaction. I intentionally avoid highly nested rare-exposure PTEN contexts because the 20-per-cell minimum could make them bounded rather than informative; the new TP53-intact IFN strata are more likely to have adequate exposed cells. For direction -1 mean-difference claims, anticipated_direction -1 encodes a raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast that is negative, meaning the exposed predictor has a more negative dependency score and therefore stronger dependency. For direction -1 interaction claims, anticipated_direction -1 encodes a raw interaction that is negative, meaning the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the named subgroup than in its complement. The large-axis IFN interaction claims anticipate raw interaction 0 because IFN-gamma has so far been accepted only as a context modifier for the moderate PTEN-STAT3 axis, not for the large axes. The NFE2L2 interaction uses direction +1 because accepted KEAP1-loss evidence corresponds to less negative NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency. The MDM2 high IFN plus 9p21-low and high research signature C direct claims test whether biologically plausible CDKN2A locus-context labels and constructed signature-C context combine with IFN context. All results would remain associations in the supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset, with no claim of causality or external generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

I intentionally defer H331 and H336 rather than run them, because they are deeply nested subgroup comparisons combining IFN-gamma with 9p21-low or high research-signature-C context and therefore have higher risk of sparse exposed cells and less general interpretability; the broader H327 and H330 comparisons already test the IFN context for CDKN2A-loss MDM2. Interpretation will follow the same conservative benchmark used throughout the run: practically meaningful context or cross-predictor effects should be directionally consistent, generally exceed about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, and have intervals excluding zero. Small interval-crossing effects are treated as unsupported or bounded non-informative, especially in small cells. Results remain associations within this lung-cell-line CRISPR screen dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: This final discovery batch quantifies the direct PTEN-loss STAT3 association in high versus lower IFN-gamma strata, tests whether IFN-gamma modifies the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association, tests IFN-gamma specificity for the four largest dependency axes, and completes PTEN-loss specificity for DHX9 and RIT1. I used the same conservative audit rule: for these centered continuous dependency scores, an association is treated as practically and inferentially supportable when the signed estimate is materially substantial, generally at least about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, the 95% interval excludes zero, and the pattern is directionally coherent with the registered hypothesis and related context analyses. A raw 10% relative rule is difficult on this negative-centered dependency-score scale, so I used an approximately 0.10 absolute practical floor together with uncertainty and consistency. Direction convention remains important: for direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction -1 interactions, positive signed interaction means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the named subgroup than in its complement. For the accepted reversed KEAP1-NFE2L2 axis, direction +1 means positive estimates encode less negative NFE2L2 scores after KEAP1 loss, i.e. weaker measured dependency. H325 gives +0.428 [0.326, 0.529] in high IFN-gamma cells and H326 gives +0.207 [0.148, 0.266] in lower/equal IFN-gamma cells; both are large, exclude zero, and support a genuine PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency in both IFN strata. The high-minus-lower difference is roughly 0.221, which coheres with the accepted H320 IFN-gamma interaction +0.221 [0.104, 0.338]. H328 +0.439 [0.326, 0.553] and H329 +0.227 [0.158, 0.295] within TP53-intact cells show that this context effect is not driven only by TP53-loss cells; PTEN-loss cells in high IFN-gamma context have much stronger measured STAT3 dependency than PTEN-loss cells in lower IFN context, while the association also remains present and meaningful in TP53-intact lower IFN cells. These direct estimates justify closing H320 as internally quantified, though it remains an association rather than a causal IFN-gamma effect. H327 gives a signed IFN-gamma interaction for CDKN2A-loss MDM2 of -0.060 [-0.150, 0.030], and H330 gives a direct TP53-intact high IFN estimate of +0.050 [-0.036, 0.137]. Neither is large enough or precise enough to support IFN-gamma as a context modifier for the CDKN2A-MDM2 axis; I reject these as unsupported, not as precise nulls. The upper bounds still permit modest effects, so external validation would be needed to clarify those strata. H332-H335 test IFN-gamma interactions for TP53-USP7, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, and KEAP1-NFE2L2. All are near zero and interval-crossing: +0.00189 [-0.0446, 0.0483], -0.0274 [-0.0706, 0.0158], +0.0240 [-0.0357, 0.0838], and -0.0060 [-0.0516, 0.0396], respectively. These do not support meaningful IFN-gamma modification of the large axes. H291 and H292 give +0.00229? actually signed -0.00229 [-0.0256, 0.0211] for DHX9 and +0.00991 [-0.0139, 0.0337] for RIT1; both are tiny, cross zero, and support no PTEN-loss association. A minor coding concern is that H326 and H329 used IFN-gamma <= 0.5, so if exact values equal 0.5 occur they overlap slightly with the >= 0.5 strata; this is unlikely to materially affect conclusions because the direct estimates and H320 interaction are large, coherent, and not dependent on boundary ties. Remaining limitations are multiplicity across many context tests, possible confounding or collider-like selection in observational strata, construction of IFN-gamma and other signature predictors without assigned causal biology, and lung-cell-line dataset specificity. No independent validation request is possible because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. The accepted pattern is therefore: very large robust USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, and reversed NFE2L2 associations; moderate PTEN-STAT3 association with accepted IFN-gamma context dependence; moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 association without IFN-gamma-specific support; and no support for IFN-gamma modification of the large axes or for PTEN loss altering DHX9 or RIT1.

The IFN context is not causal and may reflect measured biology, collinearity, or selection effects. The moderate CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association remains supported overall, with context modification mainly supported by 9p21-low and signature-C-containing contexts, not by IFN-gamma. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 and is rejected or small for DHX9, RIT1, MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, BRAF. TP53 loss is selective for USP7; SMARCA4 loss selective for SMARCA2; MSI-high selective for WRN; KEAP1 loss selective for reversed NFE2L2; CDKN2A loss selective for MDM2. IFN-gamma does not meaningfully modify the four large axes. Research markers D, E, and F are largely non-informative.

Unresolved: H99 PTEN-STAT3 batch A discovery positive but validation interval crosses zero; keep unresolved closed. Several deeply nested technical or signature-context threads remain unresolved due to exhausted analysis/validation capacity. IFN-gamma and research signature contexts are constructed measured context labels, not mechanistic claims.

Most informative next analysis: adequately powered external pre-specified validation of the four large axes and especially PTEN-STAT3 context dependencies and CDKN2A-MDM2 9p21/signature-C dependencies, stratified by TP53 status where feasible. External mechanistic perturbation is required for causal inference."

record.narrative:
No new validation was released and no response deadlines are listed; assessments_due is empty and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. I therefore register no new proposals or assessments, and the controller maintained accepted claim set remains unchanged. This synthesis is a final within-dataset scientific report for the supplied 2000-sample lung-cell-line CRISPR dependency dataset. All conclusions are associations among measured variables in this dataset and do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability.

Interpretive benchmark: dependency scores are signed continuous values with more negative scores indicating stronger dependency. The supplied generic 10% relative threshold is unstable on this negative-centered scale, especially because dependency means are near -0.25 to -0.30. I therefore treated results as practically supportable when the signed estimate was materially large, generally at least about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, the interval excluded zero, and the sign was coherent with the registered hypothesis and related context analyses. Direction convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction -1 interactions, a positive signed interaction means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the named subgroup than in its complement. For accepted direction +1 NFE2L2/KEAP1 claims, a positive signed estimate means KEAP1-loss cells have less negative NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency.

Supported large associations:
1. TP53 non-loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss. Discovery H6/R6 is +0.802 [0.782,0.822] and independent validation R50 is +0.811 [0.782,0.841]. This is far above the practical benchmark. The association persists in adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma strata, adherent culture, library strata, screen-quality strata, aneuploidy strata, MYC-amplified cells, KEAP1-loss cells, EMT-high cells, high and low research-signature-A contexts, and low-serum media. Formal interactions for many modifiers were unsupported, so this is a broad robust association rather than a narrow context-specific one.
2. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4 non-loss. Discovery H7/R7 is +0.784 [0.765,0.803] and validation R13 is +0.805 [0.774,0.836]. This is a very large synthetic-lethality-like association in this dataset. It is retained across ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-non-loss cells, lineage subtype, culture, library, screen-quality strata, batch, STK11-loss cells, stemness, ploidy, and signature-A contexts. ARID1A loss alone is rejected for SMARCA2 H8/R8, and formal ARID1A interaction is unsupported H16/R16 with validation R77.
3. MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency than MSI-stable/low. Discovery H9/R9 is +0.790 [0.760,0.819] and validation R63 is +0.790 [0.736,0.843]. The association is retained across mutation-burden strata, TP53 strata, lineage, library, culture, screen-quality strata, BRCA2-loss exclusion, hypoxia, and signature-A contexts. Some high-stratum exposed cells are small, so certain nested contexts are directionally robust but less precise.
4. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker measured NFE2L2 dependency, operationalized as less negative scores. The accepted reversed claim H13/R10 is +0.796 [0.776,0.816] and validation R38 is +0.802 [0.775,0.829]. The original direction -1 H10 was correctly rejected because the raw measured contrast is in the opposite direction under the dependency-score convention. The KEAP1-NFE2L2 pattern is retained across TP53 strata, lineage, STK11-loss cells, library, culture, batch, screen-quality strata, IFN-gamma strata, and signature-A contexts.

Supported moderate context-sensitive associations:
5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Overall H94/R75 is +0.267 [0.215,0.319] and validation R76 is +0.292 [0.213,0.370]. This is well above the 0.10 absolute practical benchmark and is the strongest non-driver-matched association in the run. Direct IFN-gamma strata quantify the context pattern: high IFN-gamma H325/R300 is +0.428 [0.326,0.529], and lower/equal IFN-gamma H326/R301 is +0.207 [0.148,0.266]. The formal IFN-gamma interaction H320/R290 is +0.221 [0.104,0.338]. Within TP53-intact cells, H328/R303 is +0.439 [0.326,0.553] in high IFN-gamma cells and H329/R304 is +0.227 [0.158,0.295] in lower/equal IFN-gamma cells. Therefore PTEN-loss cells have a genuine STAT3 dependency association in both IFN strata, but the association is stronger in the high IFN-gamma context. This remains an association with a constructed measured assay, not proof that IFN-gamma signaling causes the effect.
Other contexts are also consistent with measurable attenuation or amplification. High research-signature-A context shows a much larger direct PTEN-loss STAT3 effect, H240/R204 +0.604 [0.513,0.695], with interaction H237/R201 +0.489 [0.385,0.593], whereas lower/equal signature-A is smaller but supported, H241/R205 +0.115 [0.065,0.165]. High research-signature-B attenuates the effect: high signature-B direct H206/R179 is +0.018 [-0.025,0.061], lower/equal signature-B direct H207/R180 is +0.392 [0.327,0.457], and the attenuation interaction is accepted in the signed reversed form H205/R177 +0.411 [0.333,0.488]. High research-signature-C direct effect is smaller but still supported, H259/R226 +0.156 [0.071,0.242], versus lower/equal C H260/R227 +0.319 [0.255,0.384], with accepted attenuation interaction H258/R221 +0.163 [0.056,0.270]. These signature assays are constructed arbitrary assays with no assigned biological pathway; they are context labels, not mechanistic claims.
6. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Overall H154/R129 is +0.117 [0.082,0.152] and validation R141 is +0.114 [0.067,0.161]. The association is present in TP53-intact cells, with internal validation also positive, and present but less precise in TP53-loss cells. It is larger in 9p21-low contexts, H166/R143 +0.135 [0.091,0.179] with validation R154 +0.110 [0.036,0.184]. Context modification by constructed signatures is more apparent: high research-signature-C direct H238/R202 is +0.390 [0.304,0.475], lower/equal signature-C direct H239/R203 is near null, and the high-C interaction H236/R200 is +0.388 [0.300,0.476]. Nested signature combinations show larger but smaller-cell estimates, such as high B plus high C H242/R210 +0.765 [0.692,0.838] with 39 exposed cells, lower B high C H243/R211 +0.207 [0.107,0.307], high B high A H244/R212 +0.304 [0.176,0.432], and high C low A H266/R233 +0.333 [0.230,0.437]. In contrast, high B low C H245/R213 +0.024 [-0.015,0.064], high A low C H265/R232 -0.010 [-0.057,0.038], and low C low A H267/R238 +0.007 [-0.019,0.032] are not supported. MTAP loss does not provide a robust independent MDM2 signal after conditioning on CDKN2A loss, for example H148/R121 and H185/R121. IFN-gamma does not support CDKN2A-MDM2 context modification: H327/R302 is -0.060 [-0.150,0.030] and H330/R305 is +0.050 [-0.036,0.137], both rejected as unsupported rather than precise nulls.

Specificity and negative findings:
Driver-matched dependency associations are not supported in this dataset. KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful KRAS dependency difference H1/R1; BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful BRAF dependency difference H2/R2; EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful EGFR dependency difference H3/R3, including in KRAS-nonmutant H19/R19 and KRAS/BRAF-nonmutant cells H45/R30; ERBB2 amplification does not show a meaningful ERBB2 dependency difference H4/R4, including in KRAS/BRAF-nonmutant cells H46/R31. PTEN loss is selective for STAT3 among the tested dependencies and is rejected or small for MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, WRN, EGFR, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, TMED10, BRAF, DHX9, and RIT1. TP53 loss is selective for USP7 and does not support a practical MDM2 or STAT3 effect. SMARCA4 loss is selective for SMARCA2 and does not support WRN or USP7 cross-over effects. MSI-high is selective for WRN and does not support DHX9, KIF18A, SMARCA2, or POLR2A cross-over effects. KEAP1 loss is selective for the reversed NFE2L2 effect and does not support USP7, SMARCA2, or WRN cross-over effects. CDKN2A loss is selective for MDM2 and is rejected for USP7, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2. Research markers D, E, and F largely behave as low-information or negative-control-like strata.

The four large axes are also not meaningfully modified by IFN-gamma. The formal IFN-gamma interactions are all near zero and interval-crossing: TP53-USP7 H332/R306 +0.00189 [-0.0446,0.0483], SMARCA4-SMARCA2 H333/R307 -0.0274 [-0.0706,0.0158], MSI-WRN H334/R308 +0.0240 [-0.0357,0.0838], and KEAP1-NFE2L2 H335/R309 -0.0060 [-0.0516,0.0396]. This increases confidence that the large associations are not merely artifacts of IFN-gamma context, although many other technical and biological modifiers were also non-modifying.

Negative findings are evidence against the registered comparisons in this dataset, not proof that effects are absent. There is substantial multiplicity, some small exposed cells, and possible selection or collider-like behavior in observational strata. Nominal small effects were rejected as not practically meaningful on the dependency-score scale.

Unresolved uncertainty:
The main unresolved validation case is H99, PTEN-loss STAT3 in screen_batch batch A. Discovery was positive +0.234 [0.125,0.342], but validation crossed zero +0.159 [-0.018,0.335]. This leaves batch A as uncertain context, not as a confirmed null. Many deeply nested technical or signature-context comparisons remain unresolved because analysis and validation capacity is exhausted, including H63, H65, H67, H69, H78-H81, H84, H228-H231, H235, H331, and H336. IFN-gamma and research signature contexts are accepted only as measured context labels; they may reflect measured biology, confounding, collinearity, or selection. The dataset is limited to lung cell lines and constructed assays, so biological mechanism and external generalizability remain unknown.

Most informative next analysis:
The highest-value next step is adequately powered external pre-specified validation. It should first retest the four large axes: TP53 status with USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss with reversed NFE2L2 dependency. The most important validation follow-up for moderate associations is PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in high research-signature-A, lower/equal research-signature-B, high research-signature-C, high IFN-gamma, and lower/equal IFN-gamma contexts, preferably stratified by TP53 status where cell counts permit. For CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency, external validation should test overall effect, TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata, 9p21-low copy-number context, and high research-signature-C or nested signature contexts. This future work should use pre-specified comparisons, adequate exposed and comparator cell counts, independent assay calibration, and multiplicity control. Mechanistic perturbation of TP53-USP7, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, KEAP1-NFE2L2, PTEN-STAT3, and CDKN2A-9p21-MDM2 biology would be required to move from association toward causality.
